1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# lantern — manage the LAN docs/app server. See README.md.
3	set -euo pipefail
4	
5	LANTERN_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")")/.." && pwd)"
6	SITES="$LANTERN_ROOT/sites"
7	APPS="$LANTERN_ROOT/apps"
8	UNIT_DIR="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/systemd/user"
9	APP_PORT_MIN=8101
10	APP_PORT_MAX=8199
11	MIN_CADDY="2.8.0" # readFile in templates
12	
13	SKILL_LINK="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/skills/lantern"
14	BIN_LINK="$HOME/.local/bin/lantern"
15	# Files add-app writes; rm-app refuses to delete anything else without --force.
16	APP_SCAFFOLD=(run.sh app.env route.caddy README.md)
17	
18	# Local settings (lantern.env, gitignored): LANTERN_PORT, LANTERN_CONTENT.
19	if [[ -f "$LANTERN_ROOT/lantern.env" ]]; then
20	  set -a
21	  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
22	  . "$LANTERN_ROOT/lantern.env"
23	  set +a
24	fi
25	LANTERN_PORT="${LANTERN_PORT:-8080}"
26	# Content repo for pages and tools that belong to no other repo (sibling of lantern by default).
27	LANTERN_CONTENT="${LANTERN_CONTENT:-$(dirname "$LANTERN_ROOT")/lantern-content}"
28	export LANTERN_ROOT LANTERN_PORT LANTERN_CONTENT
29	
30	# ---------- helpers ----------
31	
32	die() { printf 'lantern: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
33	
34	caddy_bin() { command -v caddy 2>/dev/null || true; }
35	
36	host_addr() {
37	  local ip
38	  ip="$(hostname -I 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}')"
39	  printf '%s' "${ip:-localhost}"
40	}
41	
42	url_for() { printf 'http://%s:%s/%s/' "$(host_addr)" "$LANTERN_PORT" "$1"; }
43	
44	valid_name() { [[ "$1" =~ ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$ ]]; }
45	
46	name_taken() { [[ -e "$SITES/$1" || -L "$SITES/$1" || -e "$APPS/$1" ]]; }
47	
48	unit_active() { systemctl --user is-active --quiet "$1" 2>/dev/null; }
49	
50	# PORT from an app's app.env (empty if missing).
51	app_port() {
52	  [[ -f "$1/app.env" ]] || return 0
53	  sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*PORT=["'\'']\{0,1\}\([0-9]*\).*/\1/p' "$1/app.env" | tail -n 1
54	}
55	
56	# Port in route.caddy's `import lantern-app[-keep] <name> <port>` line (empty if customised).
57	route_port() {
58	  [[ -f "$1/route.caddy" ]] || return 0
59	  awk '$1 == "import" && ($2 == "lantern-app" || $2 == "lantern-app-keep") { print $4 }' "$1/route.caddy" | tail -n 1
60	}
61	
62	app_dirs() {
63	  local d
64	  for d in "$APPS"/*/; do
65	    [[ -d "$d" ]] && printf '%s\n' "${d%/}"
66	  done
67	  return 0
68	}
69	
70	listening_ports() { ss -Htln 2>/dev/null | awk '{ sub(/.*:/, "", $4); print $4 }'; }
71	
72	port_listening() { listening_ports | grep -qx "$1"; }
73	
74	next_free_port() {
75	  local used p d
76	  used=" $(listening_ports | tr '\n' ' ') "
77	  while read -r d; do used+="$(app_port "$d") "; done < <(app_dirs)
78	  for ((p = APP_PORT_MIN; p <= APP_PORT_MAX; p++)); do
79	    [[ "$used" == *" $p "* ]] || { echo "$p"; return; }
80	  done
81	  die "no free port in $APP_PORT_MIN-$APP_PORT_MAX"
82	}
83	
84	# Validate the Caddyfile with the same env the service uses. Prints errors only.
85	validate() {
86	  local caddy out
87	  caddy="$(caddy_bin)"
88	  [[ -n "$caddy" ]] || die "caddy is not installed (see README → Setup)"
89	  if ! out="$("$caddy" validate --config "$LANTERN_ROOT/Caddyfile" --adapter caddyfile 2>&1)"; then
90	    printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E '"level":"error"|^Error' >&2 || printf '%s\n' "$out" >&2
91	    return 1
92	  fi
93	}
94	
95	version_ge() { [[ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$2" "$1" | sort -V | head -n 1)" == "$2" ]]; }
96	
97	# "deploy-notes" -> "Deploy notes"
98	title_for() { local t="${1//-/ }"; printf '%s' "${t^}"; }
99	
100	# Stub README with frontmatter: the landing page shows its title and description.
101	write_readme() { # file, name
102	  cat > "$1" <<EOF
103	---
104	title: $(title_for "$2")
105	# description: One line shown on the lantern landing page.
106	---
107	# $(title_for "$2")
108	EOF
109	}
110	
111	# Set KEY=value in lantern.env, keeping its other lines.
112	set_local() { # key, value
113	  local f="$LANTERN_ROOT/lantern.env"
114	  [[ -f "$f" ]] || printf '# Local lantern settings (gitignored).\n' > "$f"
115	  if grep -q "^$1=" "$f"; then
116	    sed -i "s|^$1=.*|$1=$2|" "$f"
117	  else
118	    printf '%s=%s\n' "$1" "$2" >> "$f"
119	  fi
120	}
121	
122	# Create the content repo on first use; print its path.
123	ensure_content() {
124	  if [[ ! -d "$LANTERN_CONTENT" ]]; then
125	    mkdir -p "$LANTERN_CONTENT/pages" "$LANTERN_CONTENT/apps"
126	    cat > "$LANTERN_CONTENT/README.md" <<'EOF'
127	# lantern content
128	
129	Pages and small tools served by lantern that don't belong to any other repo.
130	
131	- `pages/<name>/`: a site, linked from lantern's `sites/<name>` (`lantern new-site <name>`)
132	- `apps/<name>/`: code for a self-contained app; lantern's `apps/<name>/run.sh` starts it
133	
134	Nothing here is served by itself: only folders linked from lantern's `sites/` are visible on the LAN.
135	EOF
136	    touch "$LANTERN_CONTENT/pages/.gitkeep" "$LANTERN_CONTENT/apps/.gitkeep"
137	    if command -v git >/dev/null; then git -C "$LANTERN_CONTENT" init -q; fi
138	    echo "created content repo $LANTERN_CONTENT" >&2
139	  fi
140	  printf '%s\n' "$LANTERN_CONTENT"
141	}
142	
143	# Symlink $2 -> $1 unless a real file is in the way.
144	link_tool() { # target, link
145	  if [[ -e "$2" && ! -L "$2" ]]; then
146	    echo "skipped $2: a real file is in the way" >&2
147	    return 0
148	  fi
149	  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$2")"
150	  ln -sfn "$1" "$2"
151	  echo "linked $2 -> $1"
152	}
153	
154	# What linking a folder would put on the LAN: file count, size, risky-looking files.
155	scan_exposure() { # dir
156	  local dir=$1 files risky links
157	  local -a prune=( \( -name '.*' -o -name node_modules -o -name __pycache__ \) -prune -o )
158	  files="$(find "$dir" -mindepth 1 "${prune[@]}" -type f -print | wc -l)"
159	  printf 'exposes %s file(s), %s, under %s\n' "$files" \
160	    "$(du -sh --exclude='.?*' --exclude=node_modules --exclude=__pycache__ "$dir" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)" "$dir"
161	  echo "  (dotfiles, node_modules/ and __pycache__/ stay hidden)"
162	  risky="$(find "$dir" -mindepth 1 "${prune[@]}" -type f \( \
163	      -iname '*.pem' -o -iname '*.key' -o -iname '*.p12' -o -iname '*.pfx' -o -iname '*.jks' \
164	      -o -iname '*.keystore' -o -iname '*.kdbx' -o -iname 'id_rsa*' -o -iname 'id_ed25519*' \
165	      -o -iname 'id_ecdsa*' -o -iname '*.env' -o -iname '*.tfstate' -o -iname '*.tfvars' \
166	      -o -iname 'kubeconfig*' -o -iname '*.ovpn' -o -iname '*.sqlite' -o -iname '*.sqlite3' -o -iname '*.db' \
167	      -o \( \( -iname '*secret*' -o -iname '*credential*' -o -iname '*token*' -o -iname '*passw*' \) \
168	            ! -iname '*.md' ! -iname '*.html' \) \) -printf '%P\n' | sort)"
169	  if [[ -n "$risky" ]]; then
170	    echo "risky-looking files (would be readable on the LAN):"
171	    printf '%s\n' "$risky" | head -n 25 | sed 's/^/  /'
172	    (($(printf '%s\n' "$risky" | wc -l) > 25)) && echo "  …"
173	  fi
174	  # Text files under 1 MB with a URL carrying a password (rtsp://user:pass@host, …).
175	  risky="$(cd "$dir" && find . -mindepth 1 "${prune[@]}" -type f -size -1024k -print0 |
176	    xargs -0 -r grep -IlE '[[:alpha:]][[:alnum:]+.-]*://[^/:@[:space:]]+:[^/@[:space:]]+@' 2>/dev/null |
177	    sed 's|^\./||' | sort || true)"
178	  if [[ -n "$risky" ]]; then
179	    echo "files with credentials in a URL (scheme://user:password@host):"
180	    printf '%s\n' "$risky" | head -n 25 | sed 's/^/  /'
181	  fi
182	  links="$(find "$dir" -mindepth 1 "${prune[@]}" -type l -printf '%P -> %l\n' | head -n 10)"
183	  if [[ -n "$links" ]]; then
184	    echo "symlinks inside (followed when served):"
185	    printf '%s\n' "$links" | sed 's/^/  /'
186	  fi
187	  return 0
188	}
189	
190	# Link sites/<name> -> dir and print its URL.
191	link_site() { # name, dir
192	  ln -s "$2" "$SITES/$1"
193	  echo "added $1 -> $2"
194	  url_for "$1"; echo
195	}
196	
197	caddy_version() { "$1" version 2>/dev/null | awk '{ sub(/^v/, "", $1); print $1 }'; }
198	
199	# ---------- commands ----------
200	
201	cmd_add_site() {
202	  local usage="usage: lantern add-site <name> <path> [--dry-run] [--whole-repo]"
203	  local dry=0 whole=0 args=() a
204	  for a in "$@"; do
205	    case "$a" in
206	      --dry-run) dry=1 ;;
207	      --whole-repo) whole=1 ;;
208	      -*) die "$usage" ;;
209	      *) args+=("$a") ;;
210	    esac
211	  done
212	  [[ ${#args[@]} -eq 2 ]] || die "$usage"
213	  local name=${args[0]} path=${args[1]} target
214	  valid_name "$name" || die "site names are lowercase-kebab (a-z, 0-9, -): '$name'"
215	  name_taken "$name" && die "'$name' is already a site or app"
216	  [[ -d "$path" ]] || die "not a directory: $path"
217	  target="$(cd "$path" && pwd)"
218	  [[ "$target" == / || "$target" == "$HOME" ]] && die "refusing to serve all of $target"
219	  if [[ -e "$target/.git" ]] && ((!whole)); then
220	    die "$target is a whole repo: link its docs folder instead, or pass --whole-repo"
221	  fi
222	  scan_exposure "$target"
223	  if ((dry)); then
224	    echo "dry run: would add $name -> $target"
225	    return 0
226	  fi
227	  link_site "$name" "$target"
228	}
229	
230	cmd_new_site() {
231	  [[ $# -ge 1 && $# -le 2 ]] || die "usage: lantern new-site <name> [dir]"
232	  local name=$1 dir=${2:-}
233	  valid_name "$name" || die "site names are lowercase-kebab (a-z, 0-9, -): '$name'"
234	  name_taken "$name" && die "'$name' is already a site or app"
235	  [[ -n "$dir" ]] || dir="$(ensure_content)/pages/$name"
236	  if [[ -e "$dir" ]]; then
237	    [[ -d "$dir" ]] || die "not a directory: $dir"
238	    [[ -z "$(ls -A "$dir")" ]] || die "$dir is not empty: use add-site to serve an existing folder"
239	  fi
240	  mkdir -p "$dir"
241	  dir="$(cd "$dir" && pwd)"
242	  write_readme "$dir/README.md" "$name"
243	  echo "created $dir/README.md"
244	  link_site "$name" "$dir"
245	}
246	
247	cmd_content() {
248	  [[ $# -eq 0 ]] || die "usage: lantern content"
249	  ensure_content
250	}
251	
252	cmd_rm_site() {
253	  [[ $# -eq 1 ]] || die "usage: lantern rm-site <name>"
254	  local link="$SITES/$1"
255	  [[ -L "$link" ]] || die "no site symlink named '$1'"
256	  rm -- "$link"
257	  echo "removed $1 (the target folder is untouched)"
258	}
259	
260	cmd_add_app() {
261	  local usage="usage: lantern add-app <name> [port] [--keep-prefix]"
262	  local keep=0 args=() a
263	  for a in "$@"; do
264	    case "$a" in
265	      --keep-prefix) keep=1 ;;
266	      -*) die "$usage" ;;
267	      *) args+=("$a") ;;
268	    esac
269	  done
270	  [[ ${#args[@]} -ge 1 && ${#args[@]} -le 2 ]] || die "$usage"
271	  local name=${args[0]} port=${args[1]:-} dir d
272	  valid_name "$name" || die "app names are lowercase-kebab (a-z, 0-9, -): '$name'"
273	  name_taken "$name" && die "'$name' is already a site or app"
274	  if [[ -n "$port" ]]; then
275	    [[ "$port" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && ((port >= 1024 && port <= 65535)) || die "bad port: $port"
276	    while read -r d; do
277	      [[ "$(app_port "$d")" == "$port" ]] && die "port $port is already used by app $(basename "$d")"
278	    done < <(app_dirs)
279	  else
280	    port="$(next_free_port)"
281	  fi
282	  dir="$APPS/$name"
283	  mkdir "$dir"
284	
285	  cat > "$dir/app.env" <<EOF
286	# Port the app listens on (127.0.0.1 only). Must match route.caddy.
287	PORT=$port
288	EOF
289	
290	  local snippet=lantern-app prefix_note
291	  if ((keep)); then
292	    snippet=lantern-app-keep
293	    prefix_note="# The app is served under /$name/ and Caddy passes the full path through, so
294	# the app itself must serve everything under \$BASE_PATH (e.g. Streamlit
295	# --server.baseUrlPath, marimo --base-url, Dash url_base_pathname)."
296	  else
297	    prefix_note="# The app is served under /$name/ and Caddy strips that prefix, so use relative
298	# URLs (or build absolute ones from \$BASE_PATH / the X-Forwarded-Prefix header)."
299	  fi
300	
301	  cat > "$dir/route.caddy" <<EOF
302	# Proxies /$name/ to this app (see the $snippet snippet in the Caddyfile).
303	# Replace with custom Caddy directives if the app needs something else.
304	import $snippet $name $port
305	EOF
306	
307	  write_readme "$dir/README.md" "$name"
308	
309	  cat > "$dir/run.sh" <<EOF
310	#!/usr/bin/env bash
311	# Started by lantern-app@$name.service with PORT (from app.env), APP_NAME and
312	# BASE_PATH=/$name/ in the environment. Listen on 127.0.0.1:\$PORT.
313	#
314	$prefix_note
315	#
316	# Python: use uv, e.g.
317	#   exec uv run --script app.py                          # PEP 723 single file
318	#   exec uv run --project /path/to/repo flask --app pkg run --port "\$PORT"
319	set -euo pipefail
320	cd "\$(dirname "\$0")"
321	
322	# Placeholder: serves this folder. Replace with your server.
323	exec uv run --no-project python -m http.server "\$PORT" --bind 127.0.0.1
324	EOF
325	  chmod +x "$dir/run.sh"
326	
327	  echo "created apps/$name/ (port $port$( ((keep)) && echo ", prefix kept"))"
328	  if unit_active lantern; then
329	    cmd_reload >/dev/null && echo "caddy reloaded: /$name/ is routed"
330	  fi
331	  cat <<EOF
332	
333	next:
334	  1. edit apps/$name/run.sh to start your server on \$PORT
335	  2. systemctl --user enable --now lantern-app@$name
336	EOF
337	  unit_active lantern || echo "  3. lantern reload   (lantern isn't running yet)"
338	  echo
339	  url_for "$name"; echo
340	}
341	
342	cmd_rm_app() {
343	  local usage="usage: lantern rm-app <name> [--force]"
344	  local force=0 args=() a
345	  for a in "$@"; do
346	    case "$a" in
347	      --force) force=1 ;;
348	      -*) die "$usage" ;;
349	      *) args+=("$a") ;;
350	    esac
351	  done
352	  [[ ${#args[@]} -eq 1 ]] || die "$usage"
353	  local name=${args[0]} dir="$APPS/${args[0]}" extra f known
354	  [[ -n "$name" && "$name" != */* && -d "$dir" ]] || die "no app named '$name'"
355	  extra=""
356	  for f in "$dir"/* "$dir"/.[!.]*; do
357	    [[ -e "$f" || -L "$f" ]] || continue
358	    known=0
359	    for a in "${APP_SCAFFOLD[@]}"; do [[ "$(basename "$f")" == "$a" ]] && known=1; done
360	    ((known)) || extra+=" $(basename "$f")"
361	  done
362	  if [[ -n "$extra" ]] && ((!force)); then
363	    die "apps/$name has files add-app didn't create:$extra (move them out, or pass --force)"
364	  fi
365	  systemctl --user disable --now "lantern-app@$name" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
366	  systemctl --user reset-failed "lantern-app@$name" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
367	  rm -rf -- "$dir"
368	  echo "removed apps/$name (unit stopped and disabled)"
369	  if unit_active lantern; then
370	    cmd_reload >/dev/null && echo "caddy reloaded: /$name/ is no longer routed"
371	  fi
372	}

374	# Live check of one site or app (or one page of it) through the running lantern:
375	# the page answers, Markdown is rendered, and the page's same-origin links resolve.
376	cmd_check() {
377	  [[ $# -eq 1 ]] || die "usage: lantern check <name>[/<page>]"
378	  local name=${1%%/*} sub="" base="http://127.0.0.1:$LANTERN_PORT" fails=0 warns=0 port state
379	  [[ "$1" == */* ]] && sub="${1#*/}"
380	  # The page's URL path, and the directory its relative links resolve against.
381	  local page="/$name/$sub" pagedir
382	  pagedir="${page%/*}/"
383	  local g="" y="" r="" z=""
384	  [[ -t 1 ]] && g=$'\e[32m' y=$'\e[33m' r=$'\e[31m' z=$'\e[0m'
385	  ok() { printf '  %s✓%s %s\n' "$g" "$z" "$*"; }
386	  warn() { printf '  %s!%s %s\n' "$y" "$z" "$*"; warns=$((warns + 1)); }
387	  fail() { printf '  %s✗%s %s\n' "$r" "$z" "$*"; fails=$((fails + 1)); }
388	
389	  port_listening "$LANTERN_PORT" || die "nothing listening on port $LANTERN_PORT: is lantern running?"
390	  if [[ -d "$APPS/$name" ]]; then
391	    echo "App $name"
392	    port="$(app_port "$APPS/$name")"
393	    state="$(systemctl --user is-active "lantern-app@$name" 2>/dev/null || true)"
394	    if [[ -n "$port" ]] && port_listening "$port"; then
395	      ok "listening on $port (unit: ${state:-unknown})"
396	    else
397	      fail "nothing listening on ${port:-?} (unit: ${state:-unknown}; journalctl --user -u lantern-app@$name)"
398	    fi
399	  elif [[ -L "$SITES/$name" || -e "$SITES/$name" ]]; then
400	    echo "Site $name"
401	    if [[ -e "$SITES/$name" ]]; then ok "-> $(readlink -f "$SITES/$name")"; else fail "broken symlink -> $(readlink "$SITES/$name")"; fi
402	  else
403	    die "no site or app named '$name'"
404	  fi
405	
406	  local out code ctype body
407	  out="$(curl -s --max-time 15 -w '\n%{http_code} %{content_type}' "$base$page" || true)"
408	  read -r code ctype <<<"$(tail -n 1 <<<"$out")"
409	  body="$(sed '$d' <<<"$out")"
410	  if [[ "$code" == 200 ]]; then
411	    ok "GET $page → 200 ${ctype%%;*}"
412	  else
413	    fail "GET $page → ${code:-no response}$([[ "$code" == 502 ]] && echo " (app not reachable)")"
414	  fi
415	
416	  # Markdown pages (a .md, or a folder whose README is its index) come back rendered.
417	  local site_dir="$SITES/$name/$sub" md=0
418	  if [[ "$page" =~ \.(md|markdown)$ ]]; then
419	    md=1
420	  elif [[ "$page" == */ && -d "$site_dir" && ! -f "$site_dir/index.html" ]] &&
421	    [[ -f "$site_dir/README.md" || -f "$site_dir/readme.md" || -f "$site_dir/index.md" ]]; then
422	    md=1
423	  fi
424	  if ((md)) && [[ "$code" == 200 ]]; then
425	    if grep -qF '<link rel="stylesheet" href="/_shared/' <<<"$body"; then ok "Markdown rendered"; else fail "Markdown not rendered"; fi
426	  fi
427	
428	  # Same-origin links on the page (relative ones resolve against the page's folder).
429	  [[ "$code" == 200 ]] || body=""
430	  local link url lcode n=0 bad=0
431	  while read -r link; do
432	    [[ -n "$link" ]] || continue
433	    link="${link//&/&}"
434	    link="${link%%#*}"
435	    [[ -n "$link" ]] || continue
436	    case "$link" in
437	      *://* | //* | mailto:* | data:* | javascript:* | tel:*) continue ;;
438	      /*)
439	        url="$base$link"
440	        [[ "$link" == "/" || "$link" == /_shared/* || "$link" == "/$name/"* ]] ||
441	          warn "absolute link $link leaves /$name/ (breaks unless the app is served at the root)"
442	        ;;
443	      *) url="$base$pagedir$link" ;;
444	    esac
445	    n=$((n + 1))
446	    lcode="$(curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 15 -w '%{http_code}' "$url" || true)"
447	    if [[ "$lcode" =~ ^[23] ]]; then :; else fail "link $link → ${lcode:-no response}"; bad=$((bad + 1)); fi
448	  done < <(grep -oiE '(href|src)="[^"]*"' <<<"$body" | sed -E 's/^[^"]*"//; s/"$//' | awk '!seen[$0]++' | head -n 50)
449	  ((n == 0)) || ((bad)) || ok "$n link(s) on the page resolve"
450	
451	  echo
452	  if ((fails)); then
453	    echo "$fails problem(s), $warns warning(s)"
454	    return 1
455	  fi
456	  echo "ok ($warns warning(s)): $(url_for "$name")$sub"
457	}

459	cmd_list() {
460	  local e name target port state
461	  echo "Sites:"
462	  local any=0
463	  for e in "$SITES"/*; do
464	    [[ -e "$e" || -L "$e" ]] || continue
465	    any=1
466	    name="$(basename "$e")"
467	    if [[ -L "$e" ]]; then
468	      target="$(readlink "$e")"
469	      if [[ -e "$e" ]]; then state=""; else state="  BROKEN"; fi
470	      printf '  %-20s -> %s%s\n' "$name" "$target" "$state"
471	    else
472	      printf '  %-20s (folder in lantern)\n' "$name"
473	    fi
474	  done
475	  ((any)) || echo "  (none)"
476	
477	  echo
478	  echo "Apps:"
479	  any=0
480	  while read -r e; do
481	    any=1
482	    name="$(basename "$e")"
483	    port="$(app_port "$e")"
484	    state="$(systemctl --user is-active "lantern-app@$name" 2>/dev/null || true)"
485	    printf '  %-20s port %-6s %s\n' "$name" "${port:-?}" "${state:-unknown}"
486	  done < <(app_dirs)
487	  ((any)) || echo "  (none)"
488	
489	  echo
490	  echo "Content repo: $LANTERN_CONTENT$([[ -d "$LANTERN_CONTENT" ]] || echo " (not created yet)")"
491	  echo "Served at $(url_for "" | sed 's|/*$|/|')"
492	}
493	
494	cmd_reload() {
495	  validate || die "Caddyfile is invalid; not reloading"
496	  if unit_active lantern; then
497	    systemctl --user reload lantern
498	    echo "reloaded"
499	  else
500	    echo "config is valid; lantern.service is not running (systemctl --user start lantern)"
501	  fi
502	}
503	
504	cmd_install() {
505	  local port="" caddy ver f
506	  while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
507	    case "$1" in
508	      --port) port="${2:-}"; shift 2 || die "usage: lantern install [--port N]" ;;
509	      *) die "usage: lantern install [--port N]" ;;
510	    esac
511	  done
512	
513	  caddy="$(caddy_bin)"
514	  [[ -n "$caddy" ]] || die "caddy is not installed (see README → Setup)"
515	  ver="$(caddy_version "$caddy")"
516	  version_ge "$ver" "$MIN_CADDY" || die "caddy $ver is too old; need >= $MIN_CADDY"
517	  [[ "$LANTERN_ROOT" =~ [[:space:]] ]] && die "LANTERN_ROOT must not contain spaces: $LANTERN_ROOT"
518	
519	  if [[ -n "$port" ]]; then
520	    [[ "$port" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && ((port >= 1024 && port <= 65535)) || die "bad port: $port"
521	    set_local LANTERN_PORT "$port"
522	    LANTERN_PORT=$port
523	    echo "wrote lantern.env (LANTERN_PORT=$port)"
524	  fi
525	
526	  validate || die "Caddyfile is invalid; not installing"
527	
528	  mkdir -p "$UNIT_DIR"
529	  for f in lantern.service lantern-app@.service; do
530	    sed -e "s|@LANTERN_ROOT@|$LANTERN_ROOT|g" -e "s|@CADDY@|$caddy|g" \
531	      "$LANTERN_ROOT/systemd/$f" > "$UNIT_DIR/$f"
532	    echo "installed $UNIT_DIR/$f"
533	  done
534	  systemctl --user daemon-reload
535	  link_tool "$LANTERN_ROOT/bin/lantern" "$BIN_LINK"
536	  link_tool "$LANTERN_ROOT/skill" "$SKILL_LINK"
537	
538	  if unit_active lantern; then
539	    systemctl --user restart lantern
540	    echo "restarted lantern.service"
541	  else
542	    systemctl --user enable --now lantern
543	    echo "enabled and started lantern.service"
544	  fi
545	
546	  if [[ "$(loginctl show-user "$USER" -p Linger --value 2>/dev/null)" != "yes" ]]; then
547	    echo
548	    echo "lantern stops when you log out. To keep it running:  loginctl enable-linger $USER"
549	  fi
550	  echo
551	  echo "Serving $(url_for "" | sed 's|/*$|/|')"
552	}
553	
554	cmd_doctor() {
555	  local fails=0 warns=0 g="" y="" r="" z=""
556	  [[ -t 1 ]] && g=$'\e[32m' y=$'\e[33m' r=$'\e[31m' z=$'\e[0m'
557	  ok() { printf '  %s✓%s %s\n' "$g" "$z" "$*"; }
558	  warn() { printf '  %s!%s %s\n' "$y" "$z" "$*"; warns=$((warns + 1)); }
559	  fail() { printf '  %s✗%s %s\n' "$r" "$z" "$*"; fails=$((fails + 1)); }
560	
561	  echo "Caddy"
562	  local caddy ver
563	  caddy="$(caddy_bin)"
564	  if [[ -z "$caddy" ]]; then
565	    fail "caddy not installed"
566	  else
567	    ver="$(caddy_version "$caddy")"
568	    if version_ge "$ver" "$MIN_CADDY"; then ok "caddy $ver ($caddy)"; else fail "caddy $ver is too old (need >= $MIN_CADDY)"; fi
569	    if validate 2>/dev/null; then ok "Caddyfile valid"; else fail "Caddyfile invalid: run bin/lantern reload to see errors"; fi
570	  fi
571	
572	  echo "Service"
573	  local f
574	  for f in lantern.service lantern-app@.service; do
575	    if [[ ! -f "$UNIT_DIR/$f" ]]; then
576	      fail "$f not installed; run bin/lantern install"
577	    elif cmp -s <(sed -e "s|@LANTERN_ROOT@|$LANTERN_ROOT|g" -e "s|@CADDY@|$caddy|g" "$LANTERN_ROOT/systemd/$f") "$UNIT_DIR/$f"; then
578	      ok "$f installed"
579	    else
580	      warn "$f differs from systemd/$f; run bin/lantern install"
581	    fi
582	  done
583	  if unit_active lantern; then ok "lantern.service running"; else fail "lantern.service not running (journalctl --user -u lantern)"; fi
584	  if systemctl --user is-enabled --quiet lantern 2>/dev/null; then ok "lantern.service enabled"; else warn "lantern.service not enabled (won't start at boot)"; fi
585	  if [[ "$(loginctl show-user "$USER" -p Linger --value 2>/dev/null)" == "yes" ]]; then
586	    ok "linger enabled"
587	  else
588	    warn "linger disabled: lantern stops at logout (loginctl enable-linger $USER)"
589	  fi
590	  if port_listening "$LANTERN_PORT"; then
591	    ok "port $LANTERN_PORT listening"
592	    local code
593	    code="$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "http://127.0.0.1:$LANTERN_PORT/" 2>/dev/null || true)"
594	    if [[ "$code" == 200 ]]; then ok "GET / → 200"; else fail "GET / → ${code:-no response}"; fi
595	  else
596	    fail "nothing listening on port $LANTERN_PORT"
597	  fi
598	  if grep -qs '^ENABLED=yes' /etc/ufw/ufw.conf; then
599	    warn "ufw is enabled: make sure the LAN may reach port $LANTERN_PORT, e.g. sudo ufw allow from <lan-subnet> to any port $LANTERN_PORT proto tcp"
600	  fi
601	  local link target
602	  for link in "$BIN_LINK:$LANTERN_ROOT/bin/lantern" "$SKILL_LINK:$LANTERN_ROOT/skill"; do
603	    target="${link#*:}" link="${link%%:*}"
604	    if [[ "$(readlink -f "$link" 2>/dev/null)" == "$(readlink -f "$target")" ]]; then
605	      ok "$link linked"
606	    else
607	      warn "$link is not linked to $target; run bin/lantern install"
608	    fi
609	  done
610	  if [[ -d "$LANTERN_CONTENT" ]]; then ok "content repo $LANTERN_CONTENT"; fi
611	  if [[ -n "${HTTPS_PROXY:-${https_proxy:-}}" ]] && ! grep -qsiE '^https_proxy=' "$LANTERN_ROOT/lantern.env"; then
612	    warn "your shell uses a proxy but app units won't: add HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY/NO_PROXY to lantern.env so uv can install app dependencies"
613	  fi
614	
615	  echo "Sites"
616	  local e name n=0
617	  for e in "$SITES"/*; do
618	    [[ -e "$e" || -L "$e" ]] || continue
619	    name="$(basename "$e")"
620	    n=$((n + 1))
621	    if [[ -L "$e" && ! -e "$e" ]]; then
622	      fail "$name: broken symlink -> $(readlink "$e")"
623	    elif [[ ! -L "$e" && "$name" != _* ]]; then
624	      warn "$name: is a real folder, not a symlink"
625	    elif [[ "$name" != _* ]] && ! valid_name "$name"; then
626	      warn "$name: not lowercase-kebab"
627	    fi
628	    [[ -e "$APPS/$name" ]] && fail "$name: is both a site and an app"
629	  done
630	  ok "$n site(s) checked"
631	
632	  echo "Apps"
633	  local d port rport state seen=" " na=0
634	  while read -r d; do
635	    name="$(basename "$d")"
636	    na=$((na + 1))
637	    port="$(app_port "$d")"
638	    rport="$(route_port "$d")"
639	    [[ -x "$d/run.sh" ]] || fail "$name: run.sh missing or not executable"
640	    [[ -f "$d/route.caddy" ]] || fail "$name: route.caddy missing (app is not routed)"
641	    if [[ -z "$port" ]]; then
642	      fail "$name: no PORT in app.env"
643	    else
644	      [[ "$seen" == *" $port "* ]] && fail "$name: port $port used by another app"
645	      seen+="$port "
646	      ((port >= APP_PORT_MIN && port <= APP_PORT_MAX)) || warn "$name: port $port outside $APP_PORT_MIN-$APP_PORT_MAX"
647	      [[ -n "$rport" && "$rport" != "$port" ]] && fail "$name: route.caddy proxies to $rport but app.env says $port"
648	    fi
649	    state="$(systemctl --user is-active "lantern-app@$name" 2>/dev/null || true)"
650	    if [[ "$state" == active ]]; then
651	      if [[ -n "$port" ]] && ! port_listening "$port"; then
652	        warn "$name: running but nothing listening on $port"
653	      else
654	        ok "$name: running on $port"
655	      fi
656	    else
657	      warn "$name: not running (systemctl --user enable --now lantern-app@$name)"
658	    fi
659	  done < <(app_dirs)
660	  ((na)) || ok "no apps"
661	
662	  echo
663	  if ((fails)); then
664	    echo "$fails problem(s), $warns warning(s)"
665	    return 1
666	  fi
667	  echo "all good ($warns warning(s))"
668	}
669	
670	usage() {
671	  cat <<EOF
672	usage: lantern <command> [args]
673	
674	  add-site <name> <path> [--dry-run] [--whole-repo]
675	                           serve <path> at /<name>/ (creates a symlink in sites/);
676	                           lists what becomes readable; refuses a repo root unless --whole-repo
677	  new-site <name> [dir]    create <dir> (default: content repo pages/<name>) with a stub README, serve it
678	  rm-site <name>           remove a site (the symlink only)
679	  add-app <name> [port] [--keep-prefix]
680	                           scaffold apps/<name>/ with the next free port; --keep-prefix for apps
681	                           that serve under /<name>/ themselves (Streamlit, marimo, Dash, …)
682	  rm-app <name> [--force]  stop and disable the app's unit, remove apps/<name>/
683	  check <name>[/<page>]    live check of a site or app, or one page of it: answers, Markdown
684	                           renders, same-origin links on it resolve
685	  list                     sites (-> targets) and apps (port, status)
686	  content                  print the content repo path (creates it on first use)
687	  reload                   validate the Caddyfile, then reload Caddy
688	  doctor                   check caddy, service, port, links and apps
689	  install [--port N]       install/refresh the systemd user units, link ~/.local/bin/lantern and
690	                           the Claude skill, start lantern
691	EOF
692	}
693	
694	cmd="${1:-help}"
695	shift || true
696	case "$cmd" in
697	  add-site) cmd_add_site "$@" ;;
698	  new-site) cmd_new_site "$@" ;;
699	  rm-site) cmd_rm_site "$@" ;;
700	  add-app) cmd_add_app "$@" ;;
701	  rm-app) cmd_rm_app "$@" ;;
702	  check) cmd_check "$@" ;;
703	  list | ls) cmd_list "$@" ;;
704	  content) cmd_content "$@" ;;
705	  reload) cmd_reload "$@" ;;
706	  doctor) cmd_doctor "$@" ;;
707	  install) cmd_install "$@" ;;
708	  help | -h | --help) usage ;;
709	  *) usage >&2; exit 1 ;;
710	esac

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# lantern — manage the LAN docs/app server. See README.md.
set -euo pipefail

LANTERN_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")")/.." && pwd)"
SITES="$LANTERN_ROOT/sites"
APPS="$LANTERN_ROOT/apps"
UNIT_DIR="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/systemd/user"
APP_PORT_MIN=8101
APP_PORT_MAX=8199
MIN_CADDY="2.8.0" # readFile in templates

SKILL_LINK="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/skills/lantern"
BIN_LINK="$HOME/.local/bin/lantern"
# Files add-app writes; rm-app refuses to delete anything else without --force.
APP_SCAFFOLD=(run.sh app.env route.caddy README.md)

# Local settings (lantern.env, gitignored): LANTERN_PORT, LANTERN_CONTENT.
if [[ -f "$LANTERN_ROOT/lantern.env" ]]; then
  set -a
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  . "$LANTERN_ROOT/lantern.env"
  set +a
fi
LANTERN_PORT="${LANTERN_PORT:-8080}"
# Content repo for pages and tools that belong to no other repo (sibling of lantern by default).
LANTERN_CONTENT="${LANTERN_CONTENT:-$(dirname "$LANTERN_ROOT")/lantern-content}"
export LANTERN_ROOT LANTERN_PORT LANTERN_CONTENT

# ---------- helpers ----------

die() { printf 'lantern: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }

caddy_bin() { command -v caddy 2>/dev/null || true; }

host_addr() {
  local ip
  ip="$(hostname -I 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}')"
  printf '%s' "${ip:-localhost}"
}

url_for() { printf 'http://%s:%s/%s/' "$(host_addr)" "$LANTERN_PORT" "$1"; }

valid_name() { [[ "$1" =~ ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$ ]]; }

name_taken() { [[ -e "$SITES/$1" || -L "$SITES/$1" || -e "$APPS/$1" ]]; }

unit_active() { systemctl --user is-active --quiet "$1" 2>/dev/null; }

# PORT from an app's app.env (empty if missing).
app_port() {
  [[ -f "$1/app.env" ]] || return 0
  sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*PORT=["'\'']\{0,1\}\([0-9]*\).*/\1/p' "$1/app.env" | tail -n 1
}

# Port in route.caddy's `import lantern-app[-keep] <name> <port>` line (empty if customised).
route_port() {
  [[ -f "$1/route.caddy" ]] || return 0
  awk '$1 == "import" && ($2 == "lantern-app" || $2 == "lantern-app-keep") { print $4 }' "$1/route.caddy" | tail -n 1
}

app_dirs() {
  local d
  for d in "$APPS"/*/; do
    [[ -d "$d" ]] && printf '%s\n' "${d%/}"
  done
  return 0
}

listening_ports() { ss -Htln 2>/dev/null | awk '{ sub(/.*:/, "", $4); print $4 }'; }

port_listening() { listening_ports | grep -qx "$1"; }

next_free_port() {
  local used p d
  used=" $(listening_ports | tr '\n' ' ') "
  while read -r d; do used+="$(app_port "$d") "; done < <(app_dirs)
  for ((p = APP_PORT_MIN; p <= APP_PORT_MAX; p++)); do
    [[ "$used" == *" $p "* ]] || { echo "$p"; return; }
  done
  die "no free port in $APP_PORT_MIN-$APP_PORT_MAX"
}

# Validate the Caddyfile with the same env the service uses. Prints errors only.
validate() {
  local caddy out
  caddy="$(caddy_bin)"
  [[ -n "$caddy" ]] || die "caddy is not installed (see README → Setup)"
  if ! out="$("$caddy" validate --config "$LANTERN_ROOT/Caddyfile" --adapter caddyfile 2>&1)"; then
    printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E '"level":"error"|^Error' >&2 || printf '%s\n' "$out" >&2
    return 1
  fi
}

version_ge() { [[ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$2" "$1" | sort -V | head -n 1)" == "$2" ]]; }

# "deploy-notes" -> "Deploy notes"
title_for() { local t="${1//-/ }"; printf '%s' "${t^}"; }

# Stub README with frontmatter: the landing page shows its title and description.
write_readme() { # file, name
  cat > "$1" <<EOF
---
title: $(title_for "$2")
# description: One line shown on the lantern landing page.
---
# $(title_for "$2")
EOF
}

# Set KEY=value in lantern.env, keeping its other lines.
set_local() { # key, value
  local f="$LANTERN_ROOT/lantern.env"
  [[ -f "$f" ]] || printf '# Local lantern settings (gitignored).\n' > "$f"
  if grep -q "^$1=" "$f"; then
    sed -i "s|^$1=.*|$1=$2|" "$f"
  else
    printf '%s=%s\n' "$1" "$2" >> "$f"
  fi
}

# Create the content repo on first use; print its path.
ensure_content() {
  if [[ ! -d "$LANTERN_CONTENT" ]]; then
    mkdir -p "$LANTERN_CONTENT/pages" "$LANTERN_CONTENT/apps"
    cat > "$LANTERN_CONTENT/README.md" <<'EOF'
# lantern content

Pages and small tools served by lantern that don't belong to any other repo.

- `pages/<name>/`: a site, linked from lantern's `sites/<name>` (`lantern new-site <name>`)
- `apps/<name>/`: code for a self-contained app; lantern's `apps/<name>/run.sh` starts it

Nothing here is served by itself: only folders linked from lantern's `sites/` are visible on the LAN.
EOF
    touch "$LANTERN_CONTENT/pages/.gitkeep" "$LANTERN_CONTENT/apps/.gitkeep"
    if command -v git >/dev/null; then git -C "$LANTERN_CONTENT" init -q; fi
    echo "created content repo $LANTERN_CONTENT" >&2
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$LANTERN_CONTENT"
}

# Symlink $2 -> $1 unless a real file is in the way.
link_tool() { # target, link
  if [[ -e "$2" && ! -L "$2" ]]; then
    echo "skipped $2: a real file is in the way" >&2
    return 0
  fi
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$2")"
  ln -sfn "$1" "$2"
  echo "linked $2 -> $1"
}

# What linking a folder would put on the LAN: file count, size, risky-looking files.
scan_exposure() { # dir
  local dir=$1 files risky links
  local -a prune=( \( -name '.*' -o -name node_modules -o -name __pycache__ \) -prune -o )
  files="$(find "$dir" -mindepth 1 "${prune[@]}" -type f -print | wc -l)"
  printf 'exposes %s file(s), %s, under %s\n' "$files" \
    "$(du -sh --exclude='.?*' --exclude=node_modules --exclude=__pycache__ "$dir" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)" "$dir"
  echo "  (dotfiles, node_modules/ and __pycache__/ stay hidden)"
  risky="$(find "$dir" -mindepth 1 "${prune[@]}" -type f \( \
      -iname '*.pem' -o -iname '*.key' -o -iname '*.p12' -o -iname '*.pfx' -o -iname '*.jks' \
      -o -iname '*.keystore' -o -iname '*.kdbx' -o -iname 'id_rsa*' -o -iname 'id_ed25519*' \
      -o -iname 'id_ecdsa*' -o -iname '*.env' -o -iname '*.tfstate' -o -iname '*.tfvars' \
      -o -iname 'kubeconfig*' -o -iname '*.ovpn' -o -iname '*.sqlite' -o -iname '*.sqlite3' -o -iname '*.db' \
      -o \( \( -iname '*secret*' -o -iname '*credential*' -o -iname '*token*' -o -iname '*passw*' \) \
            ! -iname '*.md' ! -iname '*.html' \) \) -printf '%P\n' | sort)"
  if [[ -n "$risky" ]]; then
    echo "risky-looking files (would be readable on the LAN):"
    printf '%s\n' "$risky" | head -n 25 | sed 's/^/  /'
    (($(printf '%s\n' "$risky" | wc -l) > 25)) && echo "  …"
  fi
  # Text files under 1 MB with a URL carrying a password (rtsp://user:pass@host, …).
  risky="$(cd "$dir" && find . -mindepth 1 "${prune[@]}" -type f -size -1024k -print0 |
    xargs -0 -r grep -IlE '[[:alpha:]][[:alnum:]+.-]*://[^/:@[:space:]]+:[^/@[:space:]]+@' 2>/dev/null |
    sed 's|^\./||' | sort || true)"
  if [[ -n "$risky" ]]; then
    echo "files with credentials in a URL (scheme://user:password@host):"
    printf '%s\n' "$risky" | head -n 25 | sed 's/^/  /'
  fi
  links="$(find "$dir" -mindepth 1 "${prune[@]}" -type l -printf '%P -> %l\n' | head -n 10)"
  if [[ -n "$links" ]]; then
    echo "symlinks inside (followed when served):"
    printf '%s\n' "$links" | sed 's/^/  /'
  fi
  return 0
}

# Link sites/<name> -> dir and print its URL.
link_site() { # name, dir
  ln -s "$2" "$SITES/$1"
  echo "added $1 -> $2"
  url_for "$1"; echo
}

caddy_version() { "$1" version 2>/dev/null | awk '{ sub(/^v/, "", $1); print $1 }'; }

# ---------- commands ----------

cmd_add_site() {
  local usage="usage: lantern add-site <name> <path> [--dry-run] [--whole-repo]"
  local dry=0 whole=0 args=() a
  for a in "$@"; do
    case "$a" in
      --dry-run) dry=1 ;;
      --whole-repo) whole=1 ;;
      -*) die "$usage" ;;
      *) args+=("$a") ;;
    esac
  done
  [[ ${#args[@]} -eq 2 ]] || die "$usage"
  local name=${args[0]} path=${args[1]} target
  valid_name "$name" || die "site names are lowercase-kebab (a-z, 0-9, -): '$name'"
  name_taken "$name" && die "'$name' is already a site or app"
  [[ -d "$path" ]] || die "not a directory: $path"
  target="$(cd "$path" && pwd)"
  [[ "$target" == / || "$target" == "$HOME" ]] && die "refusing to serve all of $target"
  if [[ -e "$target/.git" ]] && ((!whole)); then
    die "$target is a whole repo: link its docs folder instead, or pass --whole-repo"
  fi
  scan_exposure "$target"
  if ((dry)); then
    echo "dry run: would add $name -> $target"
    return 0
  fi
  link_site "$name" "$target"
}

cmd_new_site() {
  [[ $# -ge 1 && $# -le 2 ]] || die "usage: lantern new-site <name> [dir]"
  local name=$1 dir=${2:-}
  valid_name "$name" || die "site names are lowercase-kebab (a-z, 0-9, -): '$name'"
  name_taken "$name" && die "'$name' is already a site or app"
  [[ -n "$dir" ]] || dir="$(ensure_content)/pages/$name"
  if [[ -e "$dir" ]]; then
    [[ -d "$dir" ]] || die "not a directory: $dir"
    [[ -z "$(ls -A "$dir")" ]] || die "$dir is not empty: use add-site to serve an existing folder"
  fi
  mkdir -p "$dir"
  dir="$(cd "$dir" && pwd)"
  write_readme "$dir/README.md" "$name"
  echo "created $dir/README.md"
  link_site "$name" "$dir"
}

cmd_content() {
  [[ $# -eq 0 ]] || die "usage: lantern content"
  ensure_content
}

cmd_rm_site() {
  [[ $# -eq 1 ]] || die "usage: lantern rm-site <name>"
  local link="$SITES/$1"
  [[ -L "$link" ]] || die "no site symlink named '$1'"
  rm -- "$link"
  echo "removed $1 (the target folder is untouched)"
}

cmd_add_app() {
  local usage="usage: lantern add-app <name> [port] [--keep-prefix]"
  local keep=0 args=() a
  for a in "$@"; do
    case "$a" in
      --keep-prefix) keep=1 ;;
      -*) die "$usage" ;;
      *) args+=("$a") ;;
    esac
  done
  [[ ${#args[@]} -ge 1 && ${#args[@]} -le 2 ]] || die "$usage"
  local name=${args[0]} port=${args[1]:-} dir d
  valid_name "$name" || die "app names are lowercase-kebab (a-z, 0-9, -): '$name'"
  name_taken "$name" && die "'$name' is already a site or app"
  if [[ -n "$port" ]]; then
    [[ "$port" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && ((port >= 1024 && port <= 65535)) || die "bad port: $port"
    while read -r d; do
      [[ "$(app_port "$d")" == "$port" ]] && die "port $port is already used by app $(basename "$d")"
    done < <(app_dirs)
  else
    port="$(next_free_port)"
  fi
  dir="$APPS/$name"
  mkdir "$dir"

  cat > "$dir/app.env" <<EOF
# Port the app listens on (127.0.0.1 only). Must match route.caddy.
PORT=$port
EOF

  local snippet=lantern-app prefix_note
  if ((keep)); then
    snippet=lantern-app-keep
    prefix_note="# The app is served under /$name/ and Caddy passes the full path through, so
# the app itself must serve everything under \$BASE_PATH (e.g. Streamlit
# --server.baseUrlPath, marimo --base-url, Dash url_base_pathname)."
  else
    prefix_note="# The app is served under /$name/ and Caddy strips that prefix, so use relative
# URLs (or build absolute ones from \$BASE_PATH / the X-Forwarded-Prefix header)."
  fi

  cat > "$dir/route.caddy" <<EOF
# Proxies /$name/ to this app (see the $snippet snippet in the Caddyfile).
# Replace with custom Caddy directives if the app needs something else.
import $snippet $name $port
EOF

  write_readme "$dir/README.md" "$name"

  cat > "$dir/run.sh" <<EOF
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Started by lantern-app@$name.service with PORT (from app.env), APP_NAME and
# BASE_PATH=/$name/ in the environment. Listen on 127.0.0.1:\$PORT.
#
$prefix_note
#
# Python: use uv, e.g.
#   exec uv run --script app.py                          # PEP 723 single file
#   exec uv run --project /path/to/repo flask --app pkg run --port "\$PORT"
set -euo pipefail
cd "\$(dirname "\$0")"

# Placeholder: serves this folder. Replace with your server.
exec uv run --no-project python -m http.server "\$PORT" --bind 127.0.0.1
EOF
  chmod +x "$dir/run.sh"

  echo "created apps/$name/ (port $port$( ((keep)) && echo ", prefix kept"))"
  if unit_active lantern; then
    cmd_reload >/dev/null && echo "caddy reloaded: /$name/ is routed"
  fi
  cat <<EOF

next:
  1. edit apps/$name/run.sh to start your server on \$PORT
  2. systemctl --user enable --now lantern-app@$name
EOF
  unit_active lantern || echo "  3. lantern reload   (lantern isn't running yet)"
  echo
  url_for "$name"; echo
}

cmd_rm_app() {
  local usage="usage: lantern rm-app <name> [--force]"
  local force=0 args=() a
  for a in "$@"; do
    case "$a" in
      --force) force=1 ;;
      -*) die "$usage" ;;
      *) args+=("$a") ;;
    esac
  done
  [[ ${#args[@]} -eq 1 ]] || die "$usage"
  local name=${args[0]} dir="$APPS/${args[0]}" extra f known
  [[ -n "$name" && "$name" != */* && -d "$dir" ]] || die "no app named '$name'"
  extra=""
  for f in "$dir"/* "$dir"/.[!.]*; do
    [[ -e "$f" || -L "$f" ]] || continue
    known=0
    for a in "${APP_SCAFFOLD[@]}"; do [[ "$(basename "$f")" == "$a" ]] && known=1; done
    ((known)) || extra+=" $(basename "$f")"
  done
  if [[ -n "$extra" ]] && ((!force)); then
    die "apps/$name has files add-app didn't create:$extra (move them out, or pass --force)"
  fi
  systemctl --user disable --now "lantern-app@$name" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  systemctl --user reset-failed "lantern-app@$name" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  rm -rf -- "$dir"
  echo "removed apps/$name (unit stopped and disabled)"
  if unit_active lantern; then
    cmd_reload >/dev/null && echo "caddy reloaded: /$name/ is no longer routed"
  fi
}

# Live check of one site or app (or one page of it) through the running lantern:
# the page answers, Markdown is rendered, and the page's same-origin links resolve.
cmd_check() {
  [[ $# -eq 1 ]] || die "usage: lantern check <name>[/<page>]"
  local name=${1%%/*} sub="" base="http://127.0.0.1:$LANTERN_PORT" fails=0 warns=0 port state
  [[ "$1" == */* ]] && sub="${1#*/}"
  # The page's URL path, and the directory its relative links resolve against.
  local page="/$name/$sub" pagedir
  pagedir="${page%/*}/"
  local g="" y="" r="" z=""
  [[ -t 1 ]] && g=$'\e[32m' y=$'\e[33m' r=$'\e[31m' z=$'\e[0m'
  ok() { printf '  %s✓%s %s\n' "$g" "$z" "$*"; }
  warn() { printf '  %s!%s %s\n' "$y" "$z" "$*"; warns=$((warns + 1)); }
  fail() { printf '  %s✗%s %s\n' "$r" "$z" "$*"; fails=$((fails + 1)); }

  port_listening "$LANTERN_PORT" || die "nothing listening on port $LANTERN_PORT: is lantern running?"
  if [[ -d "$APPS/$name" ]]; then
    echo "App $name"
    port="$(app_port "$APPS/$name")"
    state="$(systemctl --user is-active "lantern-app@$name" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [[ -n "$port" ]] && port_listening "$port"; then
      ok "listening on $port (unit: ${state:-unknown})"
    else
      fail "nothing listening on ${port:-?} (unit: ${state:-unknown}; journalctl --user -u lantern-app@$name)"
    fi
  elif [[ -L "$SITES/$name" || -e "$SITES/$name" ]]; then
    echo "Site $name"
    if [[ -e "$SITES/$name" ]]; then ok "-> $(readlink -f "$SITES/$name")"; else fail "broken symlink -> $(readlink "$SITES/$name")"; fi
  else
    die "no site or app named '$name'"
  fi

  local out code ctype body
  out="$(curl -s --max-time 15 -w '\n%{http_code} %{content_type}' "$base$page" || true)"
  read -r code ctype <<<"$(tail -n 1 <<<"$out")"
  body="$(sed '$d' <<<"$out")"
  if [[ "$code" == 200 ]]; then
    ok "GET $page → 200 ${ctype%%;*}"
  else
    fail "GET $page → ${code:-no response}$([[ "$code" == 502 ]] && echo " (app not reachable)")"
  fi

  # Markdown pages (a .md, or a folder whose README is its index) come back rendered.
  local site_dir="$SITES/$name/$sub" md=0
  if [[ "$page" =~ \.(md|markdown)$ ]]; then
    md=1
  elif [[ "$page" == */ && -d "$site_dir" && ! -f "$site_dir/index.html" ]] &&
    [[ -f "$site_dir/README.md" || -f "$site_dir/readme.md" || -f "$site_dir/index.md" ]]; then
    md=1
  fi
  if ((md)) && [[ "$code" == 200 ]]; then
    if grep -qF '<link rel="stylesheet" href="/_shared/' <<<"$body"; then ok "Markdown rendered"; else fail "Markdown not rendered"; fi
  fi

  # Same-origin links on the page (relative ones resolve against the page's folder).
  [[ "$code" == 200 ]] || body=""
  local link url lcode n=0 bad=0
  while read -r link; do
    [[ -n "$link" ]] || continue
    link="${link//&/&}"
    link="${link%%#*}"
    [[ -n "$link" ]] || continue
    case "$link" in
      *://* | //* | mailto:* | data:* | javascript:* | tel:*) continue ;;
      /*)
        url="$base$link"
        [[ "$link" == "/" || "$link" == /_shared/* || "$link" == "/$name/"* ]] ||
          warn "absolute link $link leaves /$name/ (breaks unless the app is served at the root)"
        ;;
      *) url="$base$pagedir$link" ;;
    esac
    n=$((n + 1))
    lcode="$(curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 15 -w '%{http_code}' "$url" || true)"
    if [[ "$lcode" =~ ^[23] ]]; then :; else fail "link $link → ${lcode:-no response}"; bad=$((bad + 1)); fi
  done < <(grep -oiE '(href|src)="[^"]*"' <<<"$body" | sed -E 's/^[^"]*"//; s/"$//' | awk '!seen[$0]++' | head -n 50)
  ((n == 0)) || ((bad)) || ok "$n link(s) on the page resolve"

  echo
  if ((fails)); then
    echo "$fails problem(s), $warns warning(s)"
    return 1
  fi
  echo "ok ($warns warning(s)): $(url_for "$name")$sub"
}

cmd_list() {
  local e name target port state
  echo "Sites:"
  local any=0
  for e in "$SITES"/*; do
    [[ -e "$e" || -L "$e" ]] || continue
    any=1
    name="$(basename "$e")"
    if [[ -L "$e" ]]; then
      target="$(readlink "$e")"
      if [[ -e "$e" ]]; then state=""; else state="  BROKEN"; fi
      printf '  %-20s -> %s%s\n' "$name" "$target" "$state"
    else
      printf '  %-20s (folder in lantern)\n' "$name"
    fi
  done
  ((any)) || echo "  (none)"

  echo
  echo "Apps:"
  any=0
  while read -r e; do
    any=1
    name="$(basename "$e")"
    port="$(app_port "$e")"
    state="$(systemctl --user is-active "lantern-app@$name" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    printf '  %-20s port %-6s %s\n' "$name" "${port:-?}" "${state:-unknown}"
  done < <(app_dirs)
  ((any)) || echo "  (none)"

  echo
  echo "Content repo: $LANTERN_CONTENT$([[ -d "$LANTERN_CONTENT" ]] || echo " (not created yet)")"
  echo "Served at $(url_for "" | sed 's|/*$|/|')"
}

cmd_reload() {
  validate || die "Caddyfile is invalid; not reloading"
  if unit_active lantern; then
    systemctl --user reload lantern
    echo "reloaded"
  else
    echo "config is valid; lantern.service is not running (systemctl --user start lantern)"
  fi
}

cmd_install() {
  local port="" caddy ver f
  while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
      --port) port="${2:-}"; shift 2 || die "usage: lantern install [--port N]" ;;
      *) die "usage: lantern install [--port N]" ;;
    esac
  done

  caddy="$(caddy_bin)"
  [[ -n "$caddy" ]] || die "caddy is not installed (see README → Setup)"
  ver="$(caddy_version "$caddy")"
  version_ge "$ver" "$MIN_CADDY" || die "caddy $ver is too old; need >= $MIN_CADDY"
  [[ "$LANTERN_ROOT" =~ [[:space:]] ]] && die "LANTERN_ROOT must not contain spaces: $LANTERN_ROOT"

  if [[ -n "$port" ]]; then
    [[ "$port" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && ((port >= 1024 && port <= 65535)) || die "bad port: $port"
    set_local LANTERN_PORT "$port"
    LANTERN_PORT=$port
    echo "wrote lantern.env (LANTERN_PORT=$port)"
  fi

  validate || die "Caddyfile is invalid; not installing"

  mkdir -p "$UNIT_DIR"
  for f in lantern.service lantern-app@.service; do
    sed -e "s|@LANTERN_ROOT@|$LANTERN_ROOT|g" -e "s|@CADDY@|$caddy|g" \
      "$LANTERN_ROOT/systemd/$f" > "$UNIT_DIR/$f"
    echo "installed $UNIT_DIR/$f"
  done
  systemctl --user daemon-reload
  link_tool "$LANTERN_ROOT/bin/lantern" "$BIN_LINK"
  link_tool "$LANTERN_ROOT/skill" "$SKILL_LINK"

  if unit_active lantern; then
    systemctl --user restart lantern
    echo "restarted lantern.service"
  else
    systemctl --user enable --now lantern
    echo "enabled and started lantern.service"
  fi

  if [[ "$(loginctl show-user "$USER" -p Linger --value 2>/dev/null)" != "yes" ]]; then
    echo
    echo "lantern stops when you log out. To keep it running:  loginctl enable-linger $USER"
  fi
  echo
  echo "Serving $(url_for "" | sed 's|/*$|/|')"
}

cmd_doctor() {
  local fails=0 warns=0 g="" y="" r="" z=""
  [[ -t 1 ]] && g=$'\e[32m' y=$'\e[33m' r=$'\e[31m' z=$'\e[0m'
  ok() { printf '  %s✓%s %s\n' "$g" "$z" "$*"; }
  warn() { printf '  %s!%s %s\n' "$y" "$z" "$*"; warns=$((warns + 1)); }
  fail() { printf '  %s✗%s %s\n' "$r" "$z" "$*"; fails=$((fails + 1)); }

  echo "Caddy"
  local caddy ver
  caddy="$(caddy_bin)"
  if [[ -z "$caddy" ]]; then
    fail "caddy not installed"
  else
    ver="$(caddy_version "$caddy")"
    if version_ge "$ver" "$MIN_CADDY"; then ok "caddy $ver ($caddy)"; else fail "caddy $ver is too old (need >= $MIN_CADDY)"; fi
    if validate 2>/dev/null; then ok "Caddyfile valid"; else fail "Caddyfile invalid: run bin/lantern reload to see errors"; fi
  fi

  echo "Service"
  local f
  for f in lantern.service lantern-app@.service; do
    if [[ ! -f "$UNIT_DIR/$f" ]]; then
      fail "$f not installed; run bin/lantern install"
    elif cmp -s <(sed -e "s|@LANTERN_ROOT@|$LANTERN_ROOT|g" -e "s|@CADDY@|$caddy|g" "$LANTERN_ROOT/systemd/$f") "$UNIT_DIR/$f"; then
      ok "$f installed"
    else
      warn "$f differs from systemd/$f; run bin/lantern install"
    fi
  done
  if unit_active lantern; then ok "lantern.service running"; else fail "lantern.service not running (journalctl --user -u lantern)"; fi
  if systemctl --user is-enabled --quiet lantern 2>/dev/null; then ok "lantern.service enabled"; else warn "lantern.service not enabled (won't start at boot)"; fi
  if [[ "$(loginctl show-user "$USER" -p Linger --value 2>/dev/null)" == "yes" ]]; then
    ok "linger enabled"
  else
    warn "linger disabled: lantern stops at logout (loginctl enable-linger $USER)"
  fi
  if port_listening "$LANTERN_PORT"; then
    ok "port $LANTERN_PORT listening"
    local code
    code="$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "http://127.0.0.1:$LANTERN_PORT/" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [[ "$code" == 200 ]]; then ok "GET / → 200"; else fail "GET / → ${code:-no response}"; fi
  else
    fail "nothing listening on port $LANTERN_PORT"
  fi
  if grep -qs '^ENABLED=yes' /etc/ufw/ufw.conf; then
    warn "ufw is enabled: make sure the LAN may reach port $LANTERN_PORT, e.g. sudo ufw allow from <lan-subnet> to any port $LANTERN_PORT proto tcp"
  fi
  local link target
  for link in "$BIN_LINK:$LANTERN_ROOT/bin/lantern" "$SKILL_LINK:$LANTERN_ROOT/skill"; do
    target="${link#*:}" link="${link%%:*}"
    if [[ "$(readlink -f "$link" 2>/dev/null)" == "$(readlink -f "$target")" ]]; then
      ok "$link linked"
    else
      warn "$link is not linked to $target; run bin/lantern install"
    fi
  done
  if [[ -d "$LANTERN_CONTENT" ]]; then ok "content repo $LANTERN_CONTENT"; fi
  if [[ -n "${HTTPS_PROXY:-${https_proxy:-}}" ]] && ! grep -qsiE '^https_proxy=' "$LANTERN_ROOT/lantern.env"; then
    warn "your shell uses a proxy but app units won't: add HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY/NO_PROXY to lantern.env so uv can install app dependencies"
  fi

  echo "Sites"
  local e name n=0
  for e in "$SITES"/*; do
    [[ -e "$e" || -L "$e" ]] || continue
    name="$(basename "$e")"
    n=$((n + 1))
    if [[ -L "$e" && ! -e "$e" ]]; then
      fail "$name: broken symlink -> $(readlink "$e")"
    elif [[ ! -L "$e" && "$name" != _* ]]; then
      warn "$name: is a real folder, not a symlink"
    elif [[ "$name" != _* ]] && ! valid_name "$name"; then
      warn "$name: not lowercase-kebab"
    fi
    [[ -e "$APPS/$name" ]] && fail "$name: is both a site and an app"
  done
  ok "$n site(s) checked"

  echo "Apps"
  local d port rport state seen=" " na=0
  while read -r d; do
    name="$(basename "$d")"
    na=$((na + 1))
    port="$(app_port "$d")"
    rport="$(route_port "$d")"
    [[ -x "$d/run.sh" ]] || fail "$name: run.sh missing or not executable"
    [[ -f "$d/route.caddy" ]] || fail "$name: route.caddy missing (app is not routed)"
    if [[ -z "$port" ]]; then
      fail "$name: no PORT in app.env"
    else
      [[ "$seen" == *" $port "* ]] && fail "$name: port $port used by another app"
      seen+="$port "
      ((port >= APP_PORT_MIN && port <= APP_PORT_MAX)) || warn "$name: port $port outside $APP_PORT_MIN-$APP_PORT_MAX"
      [[ -n "$rport" && "$rport" != "$port" ]] && fail "$name: route.caddy proxies to $rport but app.env says $port"
    fi
    state="$(systemctl --user is-active "lantern-app@$name" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [[ "$state" == active ]]; then
      if [[ -n "$port" ]] && ! port_listening "$port"; then
        warn "$name: running but nothing listening on $port"
      else
        ok "$name: running on $port"
      fi
    else
      warn "$name: not running (systemctl --user enable --now lantern-app@$name)"
    fi
  done < <(app_dirs)
  ((na)) || ok "no apps"

  echo
  if ((fails)); then
    echo "$fails problem(s), $warns warning(s)"
    return 1
  fi
  echo "all good ($warns warning(s))"
}

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
usage: lantern <command> [args]

  add-site <name> <path> [--dry-run] [--whole-repo]
                           serve <path> at /<name>/ (creates a symlink in sites/);
                           lists what becomes readable; refuses a repo root unless --whole-repo
  new-site <name> [dir]    create <dir> (default: content repo pages/<name>) with a stub README, serve it
  rm-site <name>           remove a site (the symlink only)
  add-app <name> [port] [--keep-prefix]
                           scaffold apps/<name>/ with the next free port; --keep-prefix for apps
                           that serve under /<name>/ themselves (Streamlit, marimo, Dash, …)
  rm-app <name> [--force]  stop and disable the app's unit, remove apps/<name>/
  check <name>[/<page>]    live check of a site or app, or one page of it: answers, Markdown
                           renders, same-origin links on it resolve
  list                     sites (-> targets) and apps (port, status)
  content                  print the content repo path (creates it on first use)
  reload                   validate the Caddyfile, then reload Caddy
  doctor                   check caddy, service, port, links and apps
  install [--port N]       install/refresh the systemd user units, link ~/.local/bin/lantern and
                           the Claude skill, start lantern
EOF
}

cmd="${1:-help}"
shift || true
case "$cmd" in
  add-site) cmd_add_site "$@" ;;
  new-site) cmd_new_site "$@" ;;
  rm-site) cmd_rm_site "$@" ;;
  add-app) cmd_add_app "$@" ;;
  rm-app) cmd_rm_app "$@" ;;
  check) cmd_check "$@" ;;
  list | ls) cmd_list "$@" ;;
  content) cmd_content "$@" ;;
  reload) cmd_reload "$@" ;;
  doctor) cmd_doctor "$@" ;;
  install) cmd_install "$@" ;;
  help | -h | --help) usage ;;
  *) usage >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

154	# What linking a folder would put on the LAN: file count, size, risky-looking files.
155	scan_exposure() { # dir
156	  local dir=$1 files risky links
157	  local -a prune=( \( -name '.*' -o -name node_modules -o -name __pycache__ \) -prune -o )
158	  files="$(find "$dir" -mindepth 1 "${prune[@]}" -type f -print | wc -l)"
159	  printf 'exposes %s file(s), %s, under %s\n' "$files" \
160	    "$(du -sh --exclude='.?*' --exclude=node_modules --exclude=__pycache__ "$dir" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1)" "$dir"
161	  echo "  (dotfiles, node_modules/ and __pycache__/ stay hidden)"
162	  risky="$(find "$dir" -mindepth 1 "${prune[@]}" -type f \( \
163	      -iname '*.pem' -o -iname '*.key' -o -iname '*.p12' -o -iname '*.pfx' -o -iname '*.jks' \
164	      -o -iname '*.keystore' -o -iname '*.kdbx' -o -iname 'id_rsa*' -o -iname 'id_ed25519*' \
165	      -o -iname 'id_ecdsa*' -o -iname '*.env' -o -iname '*.tfstate' -o -iname '*.tfvars' \
166	      -o -iname 'kubeconfig*' -o -iname '*.ovpn' -o -iname '*.sqlite' -o -iname '*.sqlite3' -o -iname '*.db' \
167	      -o \( \( -iname '*secret*' -o -iname '*credential*' -o -iname '*token*' -o -iname '*passw*' \) \
168	            ! -iname '*.md' ! -iname '*.html' \) \) -printf '%P\n' | sort)"
169	  if [[ -n "$risky" ]]; then
170	    echo "risky-looking files (would be readable on the LAN):"
171	    printf '%s\n' "$risky" | head -n 25 | sed 's/^/  /'
172	    (($(printf '%s\n' "$risky" | wc -l) > 25)) && echo "  …"
173	  fi
174	  # Text files under 1 MB with a URL carrying a password (rtsp://user:pass@host, …).
175	  risky="$(cd "$dir" && find . -mindepth 1 "${prune[@]}" -type f -size -1024k -print0 |
176	    xargs -0 -r grep -IlE '[[:alpha:]][[:alnum:]+.-]*://[^/:@[:space:]]+:[^/@[:space:]]+@' 2>/dev/null |
177	    sed 's|^\./||' | sort || true)"
178	  if [[ -n "$risky" ]]; then
179	    echo "files with credentials in a URL (scheme://user:password@host):"
180	    printf '%s\n' "$risky" | head -n 25 | sed 's/^/  /'
181	  fi
182	  links="$(find "$dir" -mindepth 1 "${prune[@]}" -type l -printf '%P -> %l\n' | head -n 10)"
183	  if [[ -n "$links" ]]; then
184	    echo "symlinks inside (followed when served):"
185	    printf '%s\n' "$links" | sed 's/^/  /'
186	  fi
187	  return 0
188	}

322	# Placeholder: serves this folder. Replace with your server.

332	
333	next:
334	  1. edit apps/$name/run.sh to start your server on \$PORT
335	  2. systemctl --user enable --now lantern-app@$name

374	# Live check of one site or app (or one page of it) through the running lantern:
375	# the page answers, Markdown is rendered, and the page's same-origin links resolve.
376	cmd_check() {
377	  [[ $# -eq 1 ]] || die "usage: lantern check <name>[/<page>]"
378	  local name=${1%%/*} sub="" base="http://127.0.0.1:$LANTERN_PORT" fails=0 warns=0 port state
379	  [[ "$1" == */* ]] && sub="${1#*/}"
380	  # The page's URL path, and the directory its relative links resolve against.
381	  local page="/$name/$sub" pagedir
382	  pagedir="${page%/*}/"
383	  local g="" y="" r="" z=""
384	  [[ -t 1 ]] && g=$'\e[32m' y=$'\e[33m' r=$'\e[31m' z=$'\e[0m'
385	  ok() { printf '  %s✓%s %s\n' "$g" "$z" "$*"; }
386	  warn() { printf '  %s!%s %s\n' "$y" "$z" "$*"; warns=$((warns + 1)); }
387	  fail() { printf '  %s✗%s %s\n' "$r" "$z" "$*"; fails=$((fails + 1)); }
388	
389	  port_listening "$LANTERN_PORT" || die "nothing listening on port $LANTERN_PORT: is lantern running?"
390	  if [[ -d "$APPS/$name" ]]; then
391	    echo "App $name"
392	    port="$(app_port "$APPS/$name")"
393	    state="$(systemctl --user is-active "lantern-app@$name" 2>/dev/null || true)"
394	    if [[ -n "$port" ]] && port_listening "$port"; then
395	      ok "listening on $port (unit: ${state:-unknown})"
396	    else
397	      fail "nothing listening on ${port:-?} (unit: ${state:-unknown}; journalctl --user -u lantern-app@$name)"
398	    fi
399	  elif [[ -L "$SITES/$name" || -e "$SITES/$name" ]]; then
400	    echo "Site $name"
401	    if [[ -e "$SITES/$name" ]]; then ok "-> $(readlink -f "$SITES/$name")"; else fail "broken symlink -> $(readlink "$SITES/$name")"; fi
402	  else
403	    die "no site or app named '$name'"
404	  fi
405	
406	  local out code ctype body
407	  out="$(curl -s --max-time 15 -w '\n%{http_code} %{content_type}' "$base$page" || true)"
408	  read -r code ctype <<<"$(tail -n 1 <<<"$out")"
409	  body="$(sed '$d' <<<"$out")"
410	  if [[ "$code" == 200 ]]; then
411	    ok "GET $page → 200 ${ctype%%;*}"
412	  else
413	    fail "GET $page → ${code:-no response}$([[ "$code" == 502 ]] && echo " (app not reachable)")"
414	  fi
415	
416	  # Markdown pages (a .md, or a folder whose README is its index) come back rendered.
417	  local site_dir="$SITES/$name/$sub" md=0
418	  if [[ "$page" =~ \.(md|markdown)$ ]]; then
419	    md=1
420	  elif [[ "$page" == */ && -d "$site_dir" && ! -f "$site_dir/index.html" ]] &&
421	    [[ -f "$site_dir/README.md" || -f "$site_dir/readme.md" || -f "$site_dir/index.md" ]]; then
422	    md=1
423	  fi
424	  if ((md)) && [[ "$code" == 200 ]]; then
425	    if grep -qF '<link rel="stylesheet" href="/_shared/' <<<"$body"; then ok "Markdown rendered"; else fail "Markdown not rendered"; fi
426	  fi
427	
428	  # Same-origin links on the page (relative ones resolve against the page's folder).
429	  [[ "$code" == 200 ]] || body=""
430	  local link url lcode n=0 bad=0
431	  while read -r link; do
432	    [[ -n "$link" ]] || continue
433	    link="${link//&/&}"
434	    link="${link%%#*}"
435	    [[ -n "$link" ]] || continue
436	    case "$link" in
437	      *://* | //* | mailto:* | data:* | javascript:* | tel:*) continue ;;
438	      /*)
439	        url="$base$link"
440	        [[ "$link" == "/" || "$link" == /_shared/* || "$link" == "/$name/"* ]] ||
441	          warn "absolute link $link leaves /$name/ (breaks unless the app is served at the root)"
442	        ;;
443	      *) url="$base$pagedir$link" ;;
444	    esac
445	    n=$((n + 1))
446	    lcode="$(curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 15 -w '%{http_code}' "$url" || true)"
447	    if [[ "$lcode" =~ ^[23] ]]; then :; else fail "link $link → ${lcode:-no response}"; bad=$((bad + 1)); fi
448	  done < <(grep -oiE '(href|src)="[^"]*"' <<<"$body" | sed -E 's/^[^"]*"//; s/"$//' | awk '!seen[$0]++' | head -n 50)
449	  ((n == 0)) || ((bad)) || ok "$n link(s) on the page resolve"
450	
451	  echo
452	  if ((fails)); then
453	    echo "$fails problem(s), $warns warning(s)"
454	    return 1
455	  fi
456	  echo "ok ($warns warning(s)): $(url_for "$name")$sub"
457	}

519	  if [[ -n "$port" ]]; then

538	  if unit_active lantern; then
539	    systemctl --user restart lantern
540	    echo "restarted lantern.service"
541	  else
542	    systemctl --user enable --now lantern
543	    echo "enabled and started lantern.service"
544	  fi

554	cmd_doctor() {
555	  local fails=0 warns=0 g="" y="" r="" z=""
556	  [[ -t 1 ]] && g=$'\e[32m' y=$'\e[33m' r=$'\e[31m' z=$'\e[0m'
557	  ok() { printf '  %s✓%s %s\n' "$g" "$z" "$*"; }
558	  warn() { printf '  %s!%s %s\n' "$y" "$z" "$*"; warns=$((warns + 1)); }
559	  fail() { printf '  %s✗%s %s\n' "$r" "$z" "$*"; fails=$((fails + 1)); }
560	
561	  echo "Caddy"
562	  local caddy ver
563	  caddy="$(caddy_bin)"
564	  if [[ -z "$caddy" ]]; then
565	    fail "caddy not installed"
566	  else
567	    ver="$(caddy_version "$caddy")"
568	    if version_ge "$ver" "$MIN_CADDY"; then ok "caddy $ver ($caddy)"; else fail "caddy $ver is too old (need >= $MIN_CADDY)"; fi
569	    if validate 2>/dev/null; then ok "Caddyfile valid"; else fail "Caddyfile invalid: run bin/lantern reload to see errors"; fi
570	  fi
571	
572	  echo "Service"
573	  local f
574	  for f in lantern.service lantern-app@.service; do
575	    if [[ ! -f "$UNIT_DIR/$f" ]]; then
576	      fail "$f not installed; run bin/lantern install"
577	    elif cmp -s <(sed -e "s|@LANTERN_ROOT@|$LANTERN_ROOT|g" -e "s|@CADDY@|$caddy|g" "$LANTERN_ROOT/systemd/$f") "$UNIT_DIR/$f"; then
578	      ok "$f installed"
579	    else
580	      warn "$f differs from systemd/$f; run bin/lantern install"
581	    fi
582	  done
583	  if unit_active lantern; then ok "lantern.service running"; else fail "lantern.service not running (journalctl --user -u lantern)"; fi
584	  if systemctl --user is-enabled --quiet lantern 2>/dev/null; then ok "lantern.service enabled"; else warn "lantern.service not enabled (won't start at boot)"; fi
585	  if [[ "$(loginctl show-user "$USER" -p Linger --value 2>/dev/null)" == "yes" ]]; then

content.content:
# lantern

Docs, READMEs, showcases and small tools from all my repos, served on the LAN.

Open `http://<this-machine>:8080/` to see everything that's hosted.

`bin/lantern install` puts the CLI on your PATH as `lantern` (a symlink in `~/.local/bin`).

## Add a doc
Point lantern at a folder inside any repo:

```bash
lantern add-site deploy-notes ~/Projects/some-repo/docs --dry-run   # what becomes readable on the LAN
lantern add-site deploy-notes ~/Projects/some-repo/docs
# -> http://<host>:8080/deploy-notes/
lantern check deploy-notes    # index answers, README renders, links on it resolve
```

That's it, no config edits and no restart. It's just a symlink in `sites/`.
`add-site` lists the file count and any risky-looking files (keys, `*.env`, databases, …) and
refuses a whole repo root unless you pass `--whole-repo`: link the docs folder instead.

New, empty site: `lantern new-site <name> [dir]` creates `dir` with a stub `README.md` and
links it. Without a `dir` it goes in the **content repo** (below).

- Write docs in **Markdown**. They're rendered with the shared style automatically,
  with server-side syntax highlighting and a copy button on every code block.
- A folder's `README.md` (or `readme.md`, `index.md`) becomes its index page, unless the
  folder has an `index.html`. Folders with neither get a file listing.
- Need custom layout or interactivity? Write a `.html` file in the same folder and add
  `<link rel="stylesheet" href="/_shared/style.css">`.
- Relative links and images (`./img.png`, `other.md`) just work.
- Never put secrets in a hosted folder. Dotfiles (`.git`, `.env`, …), `node_modules/` and
  `__pycache__/` return 404, but everything else in the folder is readable on the LAN.

`sites/_example/` shows every feature; open `/_example/` once lantern is running.

### Optional frontmatter
```markdown
---
title: Deploy notes   # <title>, heading, landing-page card; fallback: first "# heading", then the file name
description: How we deploy   # shown on the landing page (README only)
style: paper          # use /_shared/paper.css instead of the default
scripts: [mermaid]    # load extra vendored scripts for this page
---
```

```` ```mermaid ```` blocks load mermaid automatically, so `scripts: [mermaid]` is optional.

## Add an app
For something that needs a running process (Flask, Streamlit, a small Node server):

```bash
lantern add-app my-tool            # creates apps/my-tool/ with run.sh, app.env, route.caddy, README.md
# edit apps/my-tool/run.sh to start your server on $PORT (127.0.0.1)
systemctl --user enable --now lantern-app@my-tool
lantern check my-tool
# -> http://<host>:8080/my-tool/
```

`add-app` picks the next free port in 8101–8199 and reloads Caddy if it's running (otherwise
run `lantern reload` once it is). `apps/<name>/` is a machine-local wrapper (gitignored,
like `sites/`): the app's code stays in its own repo, and `run.sh` points at it.
`lantern rm-app my-tool` stops and disables the unit and removes the wrapper.

Apps live under `/my-tool/` and Caddy strips that prefix, so **apps must use relative URLs**
(`href="static/app.css"`, `fetch("api/x")`). If an app needs absolute URLs, it gets the
prefix in `$BASE_PATH` and in the `X-Forwarded-Prefix` request header (e.g. Flask with
`ProxyFix(x_prefix=1)`, uvicorn `--root-path /my-tool`, Gradio `GRADIO_ROOT_PATH`).
Apps that serve under a base path themselves (Streamlit `--server.baseUrlPath`,
marimo `--base-url`, Dash `url_base_pathname`) need the prefix kept:
`lantern add-app my-tool --keep-prefix`.

Python apps use **uv**: a single-file app with PEP 723 metadata runs with
`exec uv run --script app.py`; an app in another repo with
`exec uv run --project /path/to/repo …`. `apps/_example-app/` is a working example.

Logs: `journalctl --user -u lantern-app@my-tool -f`.

App units don't see your shell's environment. If you reach the internet through a proxy, put
`HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY` and `NO_PROXY` in `lantern.env` (every app unit reads it), or the
first start hangs while uv downloads dependencies. `lantern doctor` warns about this.

## Content repo
Pages and small tools that don't belong to any repo live in a separate git repo,
`lantern-content` next to lantern (set `LANTERN_CONTENT=` in `lantern.env` to move it).
`lantern content` prints its path and creates it on first use:

- `pages/<name>/`: a site (`lantern new-site <name>` creates one and links it)
- `apps/<name>/`: code for a self-contained app; lantern's `apps/<name>/run.sh` starts it

Commit there as you like; lantern itself only holds the infrastructure.

## With Claude Code
`bin/lantern install` links the `lantern` skill (`skill/`) into `~/.claude/skills/`, so in any
repo you can ask Claude to "put these docs on lantern", "make a blank lantern site", "add a
page to the X site" or "run this app under lantern". It surveys, shows one proposal (name,
commands, what becomes readable on the LAN, audit findings), runs it after your go, and
finishes with `lantern check`. It never commits.

## Styles
All shared CSS lives in `_shared/`. Edit `style.css` to change the default look everywhere
(it has light and dark variants), or add a variant like `paper.css` (it `@import`s
`style.css` and overrides a few variables) and select it per page with `style: paper`.

## Other commands
```bash
lantern list           # sites and apps, with targets / ports / status
lantern check X        # live check of one site or app
lantern rm-site X      # remove a site (deletes the symlink only)
lantern rm-app X       # stop + disable an app, remove apps/X/ (--force if it holds other files)
lantern doctor         # caddy, service, port, broken links, port clashes
lantern reload         # validate + reload Caddy (only needed for new apps)
tests/smoke.sh         # curl + CLI smoke tests on a throwaway copy (or: tests/smoke.sh http://host:8080)
```

## Setup (once)
Needs **Caddy ≥ 2.8** (developed against 2.11.7). Ubuntu's own `caddy` package is too old
(2.6), so use Caddy's official apt repo (https://caddyserver.com/docs/install#debian-ubuntu-raspbian):

```bash
sudo apt install --yes debian-keyring debian-archive-keyring apt-transport-https curl
curl -1sLf 'https://dl.cloudsmith.io/public/caddy/stable/gpg.key' | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/caddy-stable-archive-keyring.gpg
curl -1sLf 'https://dl.cloudsmith.io/public/caddy/stable/debian.deb.txt' | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/caddy-stable.list
sudo chmod o+r /usr/share/keyrings/caddy-stable-archive-keyring.gpg
sudo chmod o+r /etc/apt/sources.list.d/caddy-stable.list
sudo apt update && sudo apt install caddy
sudo systemctl disable --now caddy    # the package's own system service (port 80); lantern runs its own
```

Then, as yourself:

```bash
bin/lantern install            # user units -> ~/.config/systemd/user, starts lantern on :8080
                               # (--port N to change; saved in lantern.env); links
                               # ~/.local/bin/lantern and ~/.claude/skills/lantern
loginctl enable-linger $USER   # keep running after logout / across reboots
bin/lantern doctor
```

If ufw is enabled, allow the port from the LAN only, e.g.
`sudo ufw allow from 192.168.1.0/24 to any port 8080 proto tcp`.

Port 80 instead of 8080 would need a system unit with `CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE`; not set up.

first start hangs while uv downloads dependencies. `lantern doctor` warns about this.

## Content repo
Pages and small tools that don't belong to any repo live in a separate git repo,
`lantern-content` next to lantern (set `LANTERN_CONTENT=` in `lantern.env` to move it).
`lantern content` prints its path and creates it on first use:

- `pages/<name>/`: a site (`lantern new-site <name>` creates one and links it)
- `apps/<name>/`: code for a self-contained app; lantern's `apps/<name>/run.sh` starts it

Commit there as you like; lantern itself only holds the infrastructure.

## With Claude Code
`bin/lantern install` links the `lantern` skill (`skill/`) into `~/.claude/skills/`, so in any
repo you can ask Claude to "put these docs on lantern", "make a blank lantern site", "add a
page to the X site" or "run this app under lantern". It surveys, shows one proposal (name,
commands, what becomes readable on the LAN, audit findings), runs it after your go, and
finishes with `lantern check`. It never commits.

## Styles
All shared CSS lives in `_shared/`. Edit `style.css` to change the default look everywhere
(it has light and dark variants), or add a variant like `paper.css` (it `@import`s
`style.css` and overrides a few variables) and select it per page with `style: paper`.

## Other commands
```bash
lantern list           # sites and apps, with targets / ports / status
lantern check X        # live check of one site or app
lantern rm-site X      # remove a site (deletes the symlink only)
lantern rm-app X       # stop + disable an app, remove apps/X/ (--force if it holds other files)
lantern doctor         # caddy, service, port, broken links, port clashes
lantern reload         # validate + reload Caddy (only needed for new apps)
tests/smoke.sh         # curl + CLI smoke tests on a throwaway copy (or: tests/smoke.sh http://host:8080)
```

## Setup (once)
Needs **Caddy ≥ 2.8** (developed against 2.11.7). Ubuntu's own `caddy` package is too old
(2.6), so use Caddy's official apt repo (https://caddyserver.com/docs/install#debian-ubuntu-raspbian):

```bash
sudo apt install --yes debian-keyring debian-archive-keyring apt-transport-https curl
curl -1sLf 'https://dl.cloudsmith.io/public/caddy/stable/gpg.key' | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/caddy-stable-archive-keyring.gpg
curl -1sLf 'https://dl.cloudsmith.io/public/caddy/stable/debian.deb.txt' | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/caddy-stable.list
sudo chmod o+r /usr/share/keyrings/caddy-stable-archive-keyring.gpg
sudo chmod o+r /etc/apt/sources.list.d/caddy-stable.list
sudo apt update && sudo apt install caddy
sudo systemctl disable --now caddy    # the package's own system service (port 80); lantern runs its own
```

Then, as yourself:

```bash
bin/lantern install            # user units -> ~/.config/systemd/user, starts lantern on :8080
                               # (--port N to change; saved in lantern.env); links
                               # ~/.local/bin/lantern and ~/.claude/skills/lantern
loginctl enable-linger $USER   # keep running after logout / across reboots
bin/lantern doctor
```

If ufw is enabled, allow the port from the LAN only, e.g.
`sudo ufw allow from 192.168.1.0/24 to any port 8080 proto tcp`.

Port 80 instead of 8080 would need a system unit with `CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE`; not set up.

--- name: lantern description: Publish docs, pages or small web apps on lantern, the LAN docs/app server on this machine. Use when the user wants to host, share or serve a repo's docs, a README, a showcase page or a tool "on lantern" or "on the LAN"; create a blank lantern site; add a page to a lantern site; or make an existing app run under lantern. --- # lantern Lantern (Caddy) serves folders and small apps from this machine to the work LAN at `http://://`. The `lantern` CLI does all the mechanics; `lantern help` lists its commands and `lantern list` shows what is served now. `LANTERN_ROOT` is the parent of this skill's resolved directory (`readlink -f` it); its `README.md` is the user manual. ## Jobs Name the job, then read its section before the survey. One request can hold several jobs (a blank site plus its first pages): survey them together and put them in one proposal. - **Docs**: an existing folder of docs or a README becomes a site → [sites.md](sites.md) § Existing docs - **Blank site**: a new, empty site → [sites.md](sites.md) § Blank site - **Page**: a new `.md` or `.html` page in an existing site → [sites.md](sites.md) § Pages - **App**: anything that needs a running process → [apps.md](apps.md) ## Steps 1. **Survey.** Work out every value the job needs from the repo and `lantern list`: name, folder, prefix mode, run command. The name is the repo or folder name in lowercase-kebab unless the user gave one. Run the job's audit. Done when you could run every command without asking the user anything. 2. **Proposal.** One message: the name and LAN URL; the commands you will run; the files you will create or edit; the **exposure** (below); the audit findings, each with the fix you offer. Then wait for the user's go. This is the only confirmation, so make it complete. 3. **Run** exactly what the user accepted. 4. **Check.** `lantern check `, plus `lantern check /` for each page you added, must end in `ok`. Fix and re-run until they do; anything still failing goes in the report with the error. 5. **Report.** The LAN URL, warnings still open, and the list of files you created or changed in other repos and in the content repo, all left uncommitted for the user. ## Rules - **CLI for mechanics.** Symlinks in `sites/`, the app scaffold, ports, routes and reloads go through `lantern`. In `apps//` you write only `run.sh` and `README.md`. When the CLI can't do something the job needs, put that in the report. - **Exposure.** A linked folder is readable by anyone on the LAN; only dotfiles, `node_modules/` and `__pycache__/` are hidden. Link the narrowest folder that holds the docs; a repo root (`--whole-repo`) only when the user picks it in the proposal. The proposal shows `lantern add-site --dry-run` output plus your own read of config-like files in the folder (`*.json`, `*.yaml`, `*.toml`, `*.ini`, `*.cfg`, `*.conf`): name any tokens, passwords, keys or connection strings you find. - **Offline.** Pages load JS, CSS and fonts from `/_shared/` only; the LAN may have no internet. A library missing from `$LANTERN_ROOT/_shared/vendor/` is vendored there (steps in its `README.md`) once the user accepts it in the proposal. - **Uncommitted.** Every change stays in the working tree of its repo; the user commits. - **Runtimes.** Python runs through `uv`; other languages only through the toolchain the app already uses. - **Content repo.** Pages and tools that belong to no repo live in the content repo: `lantern content` prints its path and creates it on first use. # Apps An app is a process lantern proxies at `//`. Lantern's `apps//` is a machine-local wrapper (gitignored): `run.sh` (start command), `app.env` (`PORT`), `route.caddy` and `README.md` (landing card: `title`, `description`). The systemd user unit `lantern-app@` runs `run.sh` from that folder with `PORT`, `APP_NAME` and `BASE_PATH=//` set. `$LANTERN_ROOT/apps/_example-app/` is a working example. A frontend that builds to static files is a site, not an app: build it with a relative base (Vite `base: './'`) and link the build folder ([sites.md](sites.md)). A tool that lets visitors run code (Jupyter, `marimo edit`, a shell, an eval endpoint) is out of scope: tell the user it waits on the sandboxed setup in lantern's `TODO.md` (Phase 6). ## Survey - **Entry point**: how the user runs it today (README, Makefile, scripts, `pyproject.toml`, `package.json`). - **Run command**, bound to `127.0.0.1:$PORT`: - Python goes through uv: `uv run --project …` (has `pyproject.toml`), `uv run --with-requirements /requirements.txt …`, or `uv run --script app.py` (single file with a PEP 723 header). - Other languages: the app's own toolchain, already installed. - **Load**: heavy dependencies (torch, CUDA, large models) go in the proposal with their RAM/GPU cost; the machine is shared. - **Secrets**: env files stay in the app's repo; `run.sh` sources them (`set -a; . /.env; set +a`). - **Prefix mode**: from the table below. - **Absolute URLs**: grep templates, static files and JS for root-relative URLs (`href="/`, `src="/`, `action="/`, `fetch("/`, redirects to `"/…"`). In strip mode each one leaves `//` unless the framework adds the prefix itself. - **Home**: an app with no repo of its own keeps its code in `$(lantern content)/apps//`.
