--- name: lantern description: Publish docs, pages or small web apps on lantern, the LAN docs/app server on this machine. Use when the user wants to host, share or serve a repo's docs, a README, a showcase page or a tool "on lantern" or "on the LAN"; create a blank lantern site; add a page to a lantern site; or make an existing app run under lantern. --- # lantern Lantern (Caddy) serves folders and small apps from this machine to the work LAN at `http://://`. The `lantern` CLI does all the mechanics; `lantern help` lists its commands and `lantern list` shows what is served now. `LANTERN_ROOT` is the parent of this skill's resolved directory (`readlink -f` it); its `README.md` is the user manual. ## Jobs Name the job, then read its section before the survey. One request can hold several jobs (a blank site plus its first pages): survey them together and put them in one proposal. - **Docs**: an existing folder of docs or a README becomes a site → [sites.md](sites.md) § Existing docs - **Blank site**: a new, empty site → [sites.md](sites.md) § Blank site - **Page**: a new `.md` or `.html` page in an existing site → [sites.md](sites.md) § Pages - **App**: anything that needs a running process → [apps.md](apps.md) ## Steps 1. **Survey.** Work out every value the job needs from the repo and `lantern list`: name, folder, prefix mode, run command. The name is the repo or folder name in lowercase-kebab unless the user gave one. Run the job's audit. Done when you could run every command without asking the user anything. 2. **Proposal.** One message: the name and LAN URL; the commands you will run; the files you will create or edit; the **exposure** (below); the audit findings, each with the fix you offer. Then wait for the user's go. This is the only confirmation, so make it complete. 3. **Run** exactly what the user accepted. 4. **Check.** `lantern check `, plus `lantern check /` for each page you added, must end in `ok`. Fix and re-run until they do; anything still failing goes in the report with the error. 5. **Report.** The LAN URL, warnings still open, and the list of files you created or changed in other repos and in the content repo, all left uncommitted for the user. ## Rules - **CLI for mechanics.** Symlinks in `sites/`, the app scaffold, ports, routes and reloads go through `lantern`. In `apps//` you write only `run.sh` and `README.md`. When the CLI can't do something the job needs, put that in the report. - **Exposure.** A linked folder is readable by anyone on the LAN; only dotfiles, `node_modules/` and `__pycache__/` are hidden. Link the narrowest folder that holds the docs; a repo root (`--whole-repo`) only when the user picks it in the proposal. The proposal shows `lantern add-site --dry-run` output plus your own read of config-like files in the folder (`*.json`, `*.yaml`, `*.toml`, `*.ini`, `*.cfg`, `*.conf`): name any tokens, passwords, keys or connection strings you find. - **Offline.** Pages load JS, CSS and fonts from `/_shared/` only; the LAN may have no internet. A library missing from `$LANTERN_ROOT/_shared/vendor/` is vendored there (steps in its `README.md`) once the user accepts it in the proposal. - **Uncommitted.** Every change stays in the working tree of its repo; the user commits. - **Runtimes.** Python runs through `uv`; other languages only through the toolchain the app already uses. - **Content repo.** Pages and tools that belong to no repo live in the content repo: `lantern content` prints its path and creates it on first use. # Apps An app is a process lantern proxies at `//`. Lantern's `apps//` is a machine-local wrapper (gitignored): `run.sh` (start command), `app.env` (`PORT`), `route.caddy` and `README.md` (landing card: `title`, `description`). The systemd user unit `lantern-app@` runs `run.sh` from that folder with `PORT`, `APP_NAME` and `BASE_PATH=//` set. `$LANTERN_ROOT/apps/_example-app/` is a working example. A frontend that builds to static files is a site, not an app: build it with a relative base (Vite `base: './'`) and link the build folder ([sites.md](sites.md)). A tool that lets visitors run code (Jupyter, `marimo edit`, a shell, an eval endpoint) is out of scope: tell the user it waits on the sandboxed setup in lantern's `TODO.md` (Phase 6). ## Survey - **Entry point**: how the user runs it today (README, Makefile, scripts, `pyproject.toml`, `package.json`). - **Run command**, bound to `127.0.0.1:$PORT`: - Python goes through uv: `uv run --project …` (has `pyproject.toml`), `uv run --with-requirements /requirements.txt …`, or `uv run --script app.py` (single file with a PEP 723 header). - Other languages: the app's own toolchain, already installed. - **Load**: heavy dependencies (torch, CUDA, large models) go in the proposal with their RAM/GPU cost; the machine is shared. - **Secrets**: env files stay in the app's repo; `run.sh` sources them (`set -a; . /.env; set +a`). - **Prefix mode**: from the table below. - **Absolute URLs**: grep templates, static files and JS for root-relative URLs (`href="/`, `src="/`, `action="/`, `fetch("/`, redirects to `"/…"`). In strip mode each one leaves `//` unless the framework adds the prefix itself. - **Home**: an app with no repo of its own keeps its code in `$(lantern content)/apps//`. Prefer fixes in `run.sh` (flags, env, a wrapper) over edits to the app; show any code edit as a diff in the proposal. ## Prefix - **strip** (`lantern add-app `): Caddy removes `/`; the app sees `/…` and gets the prefix in `X-Forwarded-Prefix`. For apps with relative URLs, or apps told their root path. - **keep** (`lantern add-app --keep-prefix`): the app sees the full `//…`. For frameworks that serve under a configured base path themselves. | Framework | Mode | In `run.sh` | |---|---|---| | Flask / Werkzeug | strip | `ProxyFix(app.wsgi_app, x_prefix=1)` so `url_for` adds the prefix (wrapper below) | | FastAPI / Starlette | strip | `uvicorn mod:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port "$PORT" --root-path "/$APP_NAME"` | | Gradio | strip | env `GRADIO_ROOT_PATH="/$APP_NAME" GRADIO_SERVER_NAME=127.0.0.1 GRADIO_SERVER_PORT="$PORT"`, when `launch()` doesn't hardcode them | | Streamlit | keep | `streamlit run app.py --server.address 127.0.0.1 --server.port "$PORT" --server.baseUrlPath "$APP_NAME" --server.headless true` | | marimo (`run`) | keep | `marimo run app.py --host 127.0.0.1 --port "$PORT" --base-url "/$APP_NAME" --headless` | | Dash | keep | env `DASH_URL_BASE_PATHNAME="$BASE_PATH"`, server on `127.0.0.1:$PORT` | | Django (gunicorn) | keep | env `SCRIPT_NAME="/$APP_NAME"`; `STATIC_URL` under the prefix | | anything else | strip | relative URLs only | Flask wrapper, all inside `run.sh`: ```bash cd /path/to/repo exec uv run --project . python - <<'PY' import os from werkzeug.middleware.proxy_fix import ProxyFix from app import app # the repo's Flask app object app.wsgi_app = ProxyFix(app.wsgi_app, x_prefix=1) app.run(host="127.0.0.1", port=int(os.environ["PORT"])) PY ``` ## Run 1. `lantern add-app `, with `--keep-prefix` for keep mode. 2. # Mount flags shared by add-app, add-tunnel and add-proxy. Sets the caller's `mount`
# (strip, keep or own) and `args` (the other arguments).
parse_mount() { # usage, args...
  local usage=$1 a
  shift
  mount=strip args=()
  for a in "$@"; do
    case "$a" in
      --keep-prefix) [[ "$mount" == strip ]] || die "$usage"; mount=keep ;;
      --own-port) [[ "$mount" == strip ]] || die "$usage"; mount=own ;;
      -*) die "$usage" ;;
      *) args+=("$a") ;;
    esac
  done
}

new_app_name() {
  valid_name "$1" || die "app names are lowercase-kebab (a-z, 0-9, -): '$1'"
  name_taken "$1" && die "'$1' is already a site or app"
  return 0
}

cmd_add_app() {
  local usage="usage: lantern add-app <name> [port] [--keep-prefix | --own-port]"
  local mount args
  parse_mount "$usage" "$@"
  [[ ${#args[@]} -ge 1 && ${#args[@]} -le 2 ]] || die "$usage"
  local name=${args[0]} port=${args[1]:-} d
  new_app_name "$name"
  if [[ -n "$port" ]]; then
    [[ "$port" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && ((port >= 1024 && port <= 65535)) || die "bad port: $port"
    while read -r d; do
      [[ "$(app_port "$d")" == "$port" || "$(lan_port "$d")" == "$port" ]] &&
        die "port $port is already used by app $(basename "$d")"
    done < <(app_dirs)
  else
    port="$(next_free_port "$APP_PORT_MIN" "$APP_PORT_MAX")"
  fi
  scaffold_app "$name" process "$mount" "$port"
}

cmd_add_tunnel() {
  local usage="usage: lantern add-tunnel <name> <ssh-host> <host:port> [--keep-prefix | --own-port]"
  local mount args
  parse_mount "$usage" "$@"
  [[ ${#args[@]} -eq 3 ]] || die "$usage"
  local name=${args[0]} via=${args[1]} to=${args[2]} port
  new_app_name "$name"
  [[ "$via" =~ ^[^-[:space:]][^[:space:]]*$ ]] ||
    die "bad ssh host: '$via' (user@host, ssh://user@host:port or a ~/.ssh/config alias)"
  valid_hostport "$to" || die "the tunnel target is <host>:<port>, as the ssh host sees it: '$to'"
  port="$(next_free_port "$APP_PORT_MIN" "$APP_PORT_MAX")"
  scaffold_app "$name" tunnel "$mount" "$port" "$to" "$via"
}

cmd_add_proxy() {
  local usage="usage: lantern add-proxy <name> <host:port> [--keep-prefix | --own-port]"
  local mount args
  parse_mount "$usage" "$@"
  [[ ${#args[@]} -eq 2 ]] || die "$usage"
  local name=${args[0]} up=${args[1]}
  new_app_name "$name"
  up="${up#http://}" up="${up%/}"
  valid_hostport "$up" || die "the upstream is <host>:<port> of a plain-HTTP service: '${args[1]}'"
  scaffold_app "$name" proxy "$mount" "" "$up"
}

# Write apps/<name>/: app.env, route.caddy (+ port.caddy when it has its own port),
# README.md and, unless nothing runs (proxy), run.sh. Then reload and print next steps.
scaffold_app() { # name, kind, mount, port, target (tunnel/proxy), ssh host (tunnel)
  local name=$1 kind=$2 mount=$3 port=$4 target=${5:-} via=${6:-}
  local dir="$APPS/$name" upstream=$target lan="" base_path="/$name/"
  [[ "$kind" == proxy ]] || upstream="127.0.0.1:$port"
  if [[ "$mount" == own ]]; then
    lan="$(next_free_port "$LAN_PORT_MIN" "$LAN_PORT_MAX")"
    base_path=/
  fi
  mkdir "$dir"

  case "$kind" in
    process)
      cat > "$dir/app.env" <<EOF
# Port the app listens on (127.0.0.1 only). Must match route.caddy.
PORT=$port
EOF
      ;;
    tunnel)
      cat > "$dir/app.env" <<EOF
# Local end of the ssh tunnel (127.0.0.1 only). Must match route.caddy.
PORT=$port
# run.sh forwards PORT through the ssh host TUNNEL_VIA (user@host, ssh://user@host:port
# or a ~/.ssh/config alias) to TUNNEL_TO (host:port, as the ssh host sees it).
TUNNEL_VIA=$via
TUNNEL_TO=$target
EOF

      cat > "$dir/app.env" <<EOF

# Nothing runs here, so there is no unit. Caddy goes through HTTP_PROXY from lantern.env
# unless NO_PROXY covers this host. Must match route.caddy.
UPSTREAM=$target
EOF

    cat >> "$dir/app.env" <<EOF
# Port the app is served on to the LAN, at "/". Must match route.caddy and port.caddy.
LAN_PORT=$lan
EOF
    [[ "$kind" != process ]] || printf '# The app sits at the root of its own port.\nBASE_PATH=/\n' >> "$dir/app.env"
  fi

  local snippet=lantern-app arg=$port to_what="this app"
  if [[ "$kind" == proxy ]]; then snippet=lantern-proxy arg=$upstream to_what=$upstream; fi
  if [[ "$mount" == own ]]; then
    cat > "$dir/route.caddy" <<EOF
# On lantern's main port: /$name/ redirects to port $lan, where the app is served
# (port.caddy), and HEAD /_status/$name feeds the landing page's up/down badge.
# See the lantern-own-port snippet in the Caddyfile.
import lantern-own-port $name $lan $upstream
EOF
    cat > "$dir/port.caddy" <<EOF
# Serves the app on its own port $lan, at "/" (see lantern-own-port-site in the Caddyfile).
import lantern-own-port-site $name $lan $upstream
EOF

# Proxies /$name/ to $to_what (see the $snippet snippet in the Caddyfile).
# Replace with custom Caddy directives if the app needs something else.
import $snippet $name $arg
EOF

  case "$mount" in

# URLs (or build absolute ones from \$BASE_PATH / the X-Forwarded-Prefix header)." ;;

  esac
  case "$kind" in
    process)
      cat > "$dir/run.sh" <<EOF
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Started by lantern-app@$name.service with PORT (from app.env), APP_NAME and
# BASE_PATH=$base_path in the environment. Listen on 127.0.0.1:\$PORT.
#
$prefix_note
#
# Python: use uv, e.g.
#   exec uv run --script app.py                          # PEP 723 single file
#   exec uv run --project /path/to/repo flask --app pkg run --port "\$PORT"
set -euo pipefail
cd "\$(dirname "\$0")"

# Placeholder: serves this folder. Replace with your server.
exec uv run --no-project python -m http.server "\$PORT" --bind 127.0.0.1
EOF
      ;;
    tunnel)
      cat > "$dir/run.sh" <<EOF
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Started by lantern-app@$name.service: an ssh tunnel from 127.0.0.1:\$PORT through
# \$TUNNEL_VIA to \$TUNNEL_TO (all three in app.env).
#
$prefix_note
#
# The unit has no terminal and no ssh-agent, so key login must work without a prompt:
#   ssh -o BatchMode=yes $via true
# ~/.ssh/config applies. When the link dies, ServerAlive* makes ssh exit and systemd
# starts it again.
set -euo pipefail
exec ssh -N -o BatchMode=yes -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new \\
  -o ServerAliveInterval=30 -o ServerAliveCountMax=3 \\
  -L "127.0.0.1:\$PORT:\$TUNNEL_TO" "\$TUNNEL_VIA"
EOF
      ;;
  esac
  [[ ! -f "$dir/run.sh" ]] || chmod +x "$dir/run.sh"

  local how=""
  case "$mount" in keep) how=", prefix kept" ;; own) how=", own port $lan" ;; esac
  case "$kind" in
    process) echo "created apps/$name/ (port $port$how)" ;;
    tunnel) echo "created apps/$name/ (ssh tunnel on port $port to $target via $via$how)" ;;
    proxy) echo "created apps/$name/ (proxy to $upstream$how)" ;;
  esac
  if unit_active lantern; then
    cmd_reload >/dev/null && echo "caddy reloaded: /$name/$([[ -z "$lan" ]] || echo " and port $lan") routed"
  fi
  local enable="systemctl --user enable --now lantern-app@$name"
  case "$kind" in
    process) printf '\nnext:\n  1. edit apps/%s/run.sh to start your server on $PORT\n  2. %s\n' "$name" "$enable" ;;
    tunnel) printf '\nnext:\n  1. ssh -o BatchMode=yes %s true   must work without a prompt (else ssh-copy-id)\n  2. %s\n' "$via" "$enable" ;;
    proxy) unit_active lantern || printf '\nnext:\n' ;;
  esac
  if ! unit_active lantern; then
    if [[ "$kind" == proxy ]]; then echo "  1. lantern reload   (lantern isn't running yet)"; else echo "  3. lantern reload   (lantern isn't running yet)"; fi
  fi
  echo
  public_url "$name"; echo
}

parse_mount() { # usage, args...
  local usage=$1 a

  mount=strip args=()
  for a in "$@"; do
    case "$a" in
      --keep-prefix) [[ "$mount" == strip ]] || die "$usage"; mount=keep ;;
      --own-port) [[ "$mount" == strip ]] || die "$usage"; mount=own ;;
      -*) die "$usage" ;;
      *) args+=("$a") ;;
    esac
  done
}

new_app_name() {
  valid_name "$1" || die "app names are lowercase-kebab (a-z, 0-9, -): '$1'"
  name_taken "$1" && die "'$1' is already a site or app"
  return 0
}

cmd_add_app() {
  local usage="usage: lantern add-app <name> [port] [--keep-prefix | --own-port]"
  local mount args
  parse_mount "$usage" "$@"

    done < <(app_dirs)
  else

  fi

}

cmd_add_tunnel() {
  local usage="usage: lantern add-tunnel <name> <ssh-host> <host:port> [--keep-prefix | --own-port]"
  local mount args
  parse_mount "$usage" "$@"

}

cmd_add_proxy() {

scaffold_app() { # name, kind, mount, port, target (tunnel/proxy), ssh host (tunnel)
  local name=$1 kind=$2 mount=$3 port=$4 target=${5:-} via=${6:-}
  local dir="$APPS/$name" upstream=$target lan="" base_path="/$name/"

    base_path=/
  fi

  case "$kind" in
    process)
      cat > "$dir/app.env" <<EOF
# Port the app listens on (127.0.0.1 only). Must match route.caddy.

EOF
      ;;
    tunnel)
      cat > "$dir/app.env" <<EOF
# Local end of the ssh tunnel (127.0.0.1 only). Must match route.caddy.

# run.sh forwards PORT through the ssh host TUNNEL_VIA (user@host, ssh://user@host:port
# or a ~/.ssh/config alias) to TUNNEL_TO (host:port, as the ssh host sees it).
TUNNEL_VIA=$via
TUNNEL_TO=$target
EOF

# The service lantern proxies to: host:port of a plain-HTTP service this machine reaches.
# Nothing runs here, so there is no unit. Caddy goes through HTTP_PROXY from lantern.env
# unless NO_PROXY covers this host. Must match route.caddy.
UPSTREAM=$target
EOF

  if [[ "$kind" == proxy ]]; then snippet=lantern-proxy arg=$upstream to_what=$upstream; fi

# Live check of one site or app (or one page of it) through the running lantern:
# the page answers, Markdown is rendered, and the page's same-origin links resolve.
cmd_check() {
  [[ $# -eq 1 ]] || die "usage: lantern check <name>[/<page>]"
  local name=${1%%/*} sub="" base="http://127.0.0.1:$LANTERN_PORT" fails=0 warns=0 port state
  [[ "$1" == */* ]] && sub="${1#*/}"
  # The page's URL path, and the directory its relative links resolve against.
  local page="/$name/$sub" pagedir
  pagedir="${page%/*}/"
  local g="" y="" r="" z=""
  [[ -t 1 ]] && g=$'\e[32m' y=$'\e[33m' r=$'\e[31m' z=$'\e[0m'
  ok() { printf '  %s✓%s %s\n' "$g" "$z" "$*"; }
  warn() { printf '  %s!%s %s\n' "$y" "$z" "$*"; warns=$((warns + 1)); }
  fail() { printf '  %s✗%s %s\n' "$r" "$z" "$*"; fails=$((fails + 1)); }

  port_listening "$LANTERN_PORT" || die "nothing listening on port $LANTERN_PORT: is lantern running?"
  if [[ -d "$APPS/$name" ]]; then
    echo "App $name"
    port="$(app_port "$APPS/$name")"
    state="$(systemctl --user is-active "lantern-app@$name" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [[ -n "$port" ]] && port_listening "$port"; then
      ok "listening on $port (unit: ${state:-unknown})"
    else
      fail "nothing listening on ${port:-?} (unit: ${state:-unknown}; journalctl --user -u lantern-app@$name)"
    fi
  elif [[ -L "$SITES/$name" || -e "$SITES/$name" ]]; then
    echo "Site $name"
    if [[ -e "$SITES/$name" ]]; then ok "-> $(readlink -f "$SITES/$name")"; else fail "broken symlink -> $(readlink "$SITES/$name")"; fi
  else
    die "no site or app named '$name'"
  fi

  local out code ctype body
  out="$(curl -s --max-time 15 -w '\n%{http_code} %{content_type}' "$base$page" || true)"
  read -r code ctype <<<"$(tail -n 1 <<<"$out")"
  body="$(sed '$d' <<<"$out")"
  if [[ "$code" == 200 ]]; then
    ok "GET $page → 200 ${ctype%%;*}"
  else
    fail "GET $page → ${code:-no response}$([[ "$code" == 502 ]] && echo " (app not reachable)")"
  fi

  # Markdown pages (a .md, or a folder whose README is its index) come back rendered.
  local site_dir="$SITES/$name/$sub" md=0
  if [[ "$page" =~ \.(md|markdown)$ ]]; then
    md=1
  elif [[ "$page" == */ && -d "$site_dir" && ! -f "$site_dir/index.html" ]] &&
    [[ -f "$site_dir/README.md" || -f "$site_dir/readme.md" || -f "$site_dir/index.md" ]]; then
    md=1

  local name=${1%%/*} sub="" main="http://127.0.0.1:$LANTERN_PORT" fails=0 warns=0 port state
  [[ "$1" == */* ]] && sub="${1#*/}"
  # base: the origin the page is served from; prefix: the path it lives under there
  # (empty for an app on its own port, which owns "/").
  local base=$main prefix="/$name" app=0 lan=""
  local g="" y="" r="" z=""
  [[ -t 1 ]] && g=$'\e[32m' y=$'\e[33m' r=$'\e[31m' z=$'\e[0m'
  ok() { printf '  %s✓%s %s\n' "$g" "$z" "$*"; }
  warn() { printf '  %s!%s %s\n' "$y" "$z" "$*"; warns=$((warns + 1)); }
  fail() { printf '  %s✗%s %s\n' "$r" "$z" "$*"; fails=$((fails + 1)); }

  port_listening "$LANTERN_PORT" || die "nothing listening on port $LANTERN_PORT: is lantern running?"
  if [[ -d "$APPS/$name" ]]; then
    local d="$APPS/$name" kind
    app=1 kind="$(app_kind "$d")" lan="$(lan_port "$d")"
    echo "App $name"
    if [[ "$kind" == proxy ]]; then
      ok "proxies to $(app_upstream "$d") (nothing runs here)"
    else
      port="$(app_port "$d")"
      state="$(systemctl --user is-active "lantern-app@$name" 2>/dev/null || true)"
      if [[ -n "$port" ]] && port_listening "$port"; then
        ok "listening on $port (unit: ${state:-unknown})$([[ "$kind" != tunnel ]] || echo ", ssh tunnel to $(app_var "$d" TUNNEL_TO)")"
      else
        fail "nothing listening on ${port:-?} (unit: ${state:-unknown}; journalctl --user -u lantern-app@$name)"
        [[ "$kind" != tunnel ]] ||
          echo "    the tunnel needs key login without a prompt: ssh -o BatchMode=yes $(app_var "$d" TUNNEL_VIA) true"
      fi
    fi
    if [[ -n "$lan" ]]; then
      local loc scode
      if port_listening "$lan"; then ok "own port $lan listening"; else fail "nothing listening on own port $lan (lantern reload)"; fi
      loc="$(curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 5 -w '%{redirect_url}' "$main/$name/" || true)"
      if [[ "$loc" == "http://127.0.0.1:$lan/" ]]; then
        ok "/$name/ redirects to port $lan"
      else
        fail "/$name/ should redirect to port $lan, got ${loc:-no redirect}"
      fi
      scode="$(curl -s -o /dev/null -I --max-time 15 -w '%{http_code}' "$main/_status/$name" || true)"
      if [[ "$scode" =~ ^[1-4] ]]; then ok "badge: HEAD /_status/$name → $scode"; else fail "badge: HEAD /_status/$name → ${scode:-no response}"; fi
      base="http://127.0.0.1:$lan" prefix=""
    fi
  elif [[ -L "$SITES/$name" || -e "$SITES/$name" ]]; then
    echo "Site $name"
    if [[ -e "$SITES/$name" ]]; then ok "-> $(readlink -f "$SITES/$name")"; else fail "broken symlink -> $(readlink "$SITES/$name")"; fi
  else
    die "no site or app named '$name'"
  fi

  # The page's URL path. Apps may redirect (to a login page, say): follow, then check there.
  local page="$prefix/$sub" out code ctype eff body shown follow=()
  ((app)) && follow=(-L --max-redirs 5)
  out="$(curl -s "${follow[@]}" --max-time 15 -w '\n%{http_code}|%{content_type}|%{url_effective}' "$base$page" || true)"
  IFS='|' read -r code ctype eff <<<"$(tail -n 1 <<<"$out")"
  body="$(sed '$d' <<<"$out")"
  shown=$page
  if [[ -n "$eff" && "$eff" != "$base$page" ]]; then
    local rest="${eff#*://}"
    if [[ "http://${rest%%/*}" != "$base" ]]; then
      shown="$page → $eff" body=""
      warn "redirects away from lantern, to $eff"
    else
      page="/${rest#*/}"
      [[ "$rest" == */* ]] || page=/
      shown="$shown → $page"
      [[ -z "$prefix" || "$page" == "$prefix/"* ]] ||
        warn "redirect to $page leaves $prefix/ (an app that needs the root: --own-port)"
    fi
  fi
  if [[ "$code" == 200 ]]; then
    ok "GET $shown → 200 ${ctype%%;*}"
  elif [[ "$code" == 401 ]] && ((app)); then
    ok "GET $shown → 401: the app asks for a login (links not checked)"
  else
    fail "GET $shown → ${code:-no response}$([[ "$code" == 502 ]] && echo " (app not reachable)")"
  fi

  # Markdown pages (a .md, or a folder whose README is its index) come back rendered.
  local site_dir="$SITES/$name/$sub" md=0
  if ((app)); then
    :
  elif [[ "$page" =~ \.(md|markdown)$ ]]; then
    md=1
  elif [[ "$page" == */ && -d "$site_dir" && ! -f "$site_dir/index.html" ]] &&
    [[ -f "$site_dir/README.md" || -f "$site_dir/readme.md" || -f "$site_dir/index.md" ]]; then
    md=1
  fi
  if ((md)) && [[ "$code" == 200 ]]; then
    if grep -qF '<link rel="stylesheet" href="/_shared/' <<<"$body"; then ok "Markdown rendered"; else fail "Markdown not rendered"; fi
  fi

  # Same-origin links on the page (relative ones resolve against the page's folder).
  [[ "$code" == 200 ]] || body=""
  local pagedir="${page%%\?*}" link url lcode n=0 bad=0
  pagedir="${pagedir%/*}/"
  while read -r link; do
    [[ -n "$link" ]] || continue
    link="${link//&/&}"
    link="${link%%#*}"
    [[ -n "$link" ]] || continue
    case "$link" in
      *://* | //* | mailto:* | data:* | javascript:* | tel:*) continue ;;
      /*)
        url="$base$link"
        [[ -z "$prefix" || "$link" == "/" || "$link" == /_shared/* || "$link" == "$prefix/"* ]] ||
          warn "absolute link $link leaves $prefix/ (breaks unless the app is served at the root$( ((app)) && echo ": --own-port"))"
        ;;
      *) url="$base$pagedir$link" ;;
    esac
    n=$((n + 1))
    lcode="$(curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 15 -w '%{http_code}' "$url" || true)"
    if [[ "$lcode" =~ ^[23] ]]; then :; else fail "link $link → ${lcode:-no response}"; bad=$((bad + 1)); fi
  done < <(grep -oiE '(href|src)="[^"]*"' <<<"$body" | sed -E 's/^[^"]*"//; s/"$//' | awk '!seen[$0]++' | head -n 50)
  ((n == 0)) || ((bad)) || ok "$n link(s) on the page resolve"

  echo
  if ((fails)); then
    echo "$fails problem(s), $warns warning(s)"
    return 1
  fi
  echo "ok ($warns warning(s)): $(public_url "$name")$sub"
}

cmd_list() {
  local e name target port state lan kind extra
  echo "Sites:"
  local any=0
  for e in "$SITES"/*; do
    [[ -e "$e" || -L "$e" ]] || continue
    any=1
    name="$(basename "$e")"
    if [[ -L "$e" ]]; then
      target="$(readlink "$e")"
      if [[ -e "$e" ]]; then state=""; else state="  BROKEN"; fi
      printf '  %-20s -> %s%s\n' "$name" "$target" "$state"
    else
      printf '  %-20s (folder in lantern)\n' "$name"
    fi
  done
  ((any)) || echo "  (none)"

  echo
  echo "Apps:"
  any=0
  while read -r e; do
    any=1
    name="$(basename "$e")"
    port="$(app_port "$e")" lan="$(lan_port "$e")" kind="$(app_kind "$e")" extra=""
    state="$(systemctl --user is-active "lantern-app@$name" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    case "$kind" in
      tunnel) extra="ssh tunnel to $(app_var "$e" TUNNEL_TO) via $(app_var "$e" TUNNEL_VIA)" ;;
      proxy) port="-" state="-" extra="proxy to $(app_upstream "$e")" ;;
    esac
    [[ -z "$lan" ]] || extra+="${extra:+, }own port $lan"
    printf '  %-20s port %-6s %s%s\n' "$name" "${port:-?}" "${state:-unknown}" "${extra:+   $extra}"
  done < <(app_dirs)
  ((any)) || echo "  (none)"

  echo
  echo "Content repo: $LANTERN_CONTENT$([[ -d "$LANTERN_CONTENT" ]] || echo " (not created yet)")"
  echo "Served at $(url_for "" | sed 's|/*$|/|')"
}

'''
s=s[:start]+new+s[end:]
open(p,'w').write(s)
PY
bash -n bin/lantern && echo syntax ok

    kind="$(app_kind "$d")" port="$(app_port "$d")" lan="$(lan_port "$d")"
    up="$(app_upstream "$d")" rup="$(route_upstream "$d")"
    [[ -f "$d/route.caddy" ]] || fail "$name: route.caddy missing (app is not routed)"
    if [[ "$kind" == proxy ]]; then
      valid_hostport "$up" || fail "$name: UPSTREAM is not <host>:<port>: $up"
    else
      [[ -x "$d/run.sh" ]] || fail "$name: run.sh missing or not executable"
      if [[ -z "$port" ]]; then
        fail "$name: no PORT in app.env"
      else
        [[ "$seen" == *" $port "* ]] && fail "$name: port $port used by another app"
        seen+="$port "
        ((port >= APP_PORT_MIN && port <= APP_PORT_MAX)) || warn "$name: port $port outside $APP_PORT_MIN-$APP_PORT_MAX"
      fi
    fi
    [[ -n "$rup" && -n "$up" && "$rup" != "$up" ]] && fail "$name: route.caddy proxies to $rup but app.env says $up"
    if [[ -n "$lan" ]]; then
      [[ "$seenlan$seen" == *" $lan "* || "$lan" == "$LANTERN_PORT" ]] && fail "$name: own port $lan is used twice"
      seenlan+="$lan "
      ((lan >= LAN_PORT_MIN && lan <= LAN_PORT_MAX)) || warn "$name: own port $lan outside $LAN_PORT_MIN-$LAN_PORT_MAX"
      pl="$(caddy_lan_port "$d/port.caddy")"
      if [[ ! -f "$d/port.caddy" ]]; then
        fail "$name: LAN_PORT is set but port.caddy is missing"
      elif [[ -n "$pl" && "$pl" != "$lan" ]]; then
        fail "$name: port.caddy serves port $pl but app.env says $lan"
      fi
      pl="$(caddy_lan_port "$d/route.caddy")"
      [[ -n "$pl" && "$pl" != "$lan" ]] && fail "$name: route.caddy redirects to port $pl but app.env says $lan"
      unit_active lantern && ! port_listening "$lan" && warn "$name: nothing listening on own port $lan (lantern reload)"
    elif [[ -f "$d/port.caddy" ]]; then
      fail "$name: has port.caddy but no LAN_PORT in app.env"
    fi
    if [[ "$kind" == proxy ]]; then
      ok "$name: proxies to $up (nothing runs here)"
      continue
    fi
    state="$(systemctl --user is-active "lantern-app@$name" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [[ "$state" == active ]]; then
      if [[ -n "$port" ]] && ! port_listening "$port"; then
        warn "$name: running but nothing listening on $port$([[ "$kind" != tunnel ]] || echo " (ssh tunnel not up yet?)")"
      else
        ok "$name: running on $port$([[ "$kind" != tunnel ]] || echo ", ssh tunnel to $(app_var "$d" TUNNEL_TO)")"
      fi
    else
      warn "$name: not running (systemctl --user enable --now lantern-app@$name)"
    fi
  done < <(app_dirs)
'''
s=s[:start]+new+s[end:]

old_ufw='''    warn "ufw is enabled: make sure the LAN may reach port $LANTERN_PORT, e.g. sudo ufw allow from <lan-subnet> to any port $LANTERN_PORT proto tcp"'''
new_ufw='''    warn "ufw is enabled: make sure the LAN may reach port $LANTERN_PORT (and $LAN_PORT_MIN-$LAN_PORT_MAX for apps on their own port), e.g. sudo ufw allow from <lan-subnet> to any port $LANTERN_PORT proto tcp"'''
assert s.count(old_ufw)==1
s=s.replace(old_ufw,new_ufw)

old_usage='''  add-app <name> [port] [--keep-prefix]
                           scaffold apps/<name>/ with the next free port; --keep-prefix for apps
                           that serve under /<name>/ themselves (Streamlit, marimo, Dash, …)
  rm-app <name> [--force]  stop and disable the app's unit, remove apps/<name>/'''
new_usage='''  add-app <name> [port] [--keep-prefix | --own-port]
                           scaffold apps/<name>/ with the next free port; --keep-prefix for apps
                           that serve under /<name>/ themselves (Streamlit, marimo, Dash, …);
                           --own-port serves the app at the root of its own LAN port (8201-8299)
                           instead, for apps with absolute URLs (device UIs, vendor dashboards)
  add-tunnel <name> <ssh-host> <host:port> [--keep-prefix | --own-port]
                           an app whose run.sh is an ssh tunnel to <host:port> as <ssh-host>
                           sees it (user@host, ssh://user@host:port or a ~/.ssh/config alias)
  add-proxy <name> <host:port> [--keep-prefix | --own-port]
                           proxy a plain-HTTP service this machine reaches; nothing runs, no unit
  rm-app <name> [--force]  stop and disable the app's unit, remove apps/<name>/'''
assert s.count(old_usage)==1
s=s.replace(old_usage,new_usage)
s=s.replace('''  list                     sites (-> targets) and apps (port, status)''','''  list                     sites (-> targets) and apps (port, status, tunnel/proxy, own port)''')
old_dispatch='''  add-app) cmd_add_app "$@" ;;'''
new_dispatch='''  add-app) cmd_add_app "$@" ;;
  add-tunnel) cmd_add_tunnel "$@" ;;
  add-proxy) cmd_add_proxy "$@" ;;'''
assert s.count(old_dispatch)==1
s=s.replace(old_dispatch,new_dispatch)
open(p,'w').write(s)

Against a running instance it adds a temporary sites/_smoke # symlink. # Apps

An app is anything lantern reverse-proxies. Lantern's `apps/<name>/` is a machine-local
wrapper (gitignored): `app.env`, `route.caddy`, `README.md` (landing card: `title`,
`description`), plus `run.sh` when something runs and `port.caddy` for an app on its own
port. The systemd user unit `lantern-app@<name>` runs `run.sh` from that folder with
`PORT`, `APP_NAME` and `BASE_PATH=/<name>/` set (`/` on its own port).
`$LANTERN_ROOT/apps/_example-app/` is a working example.

A frontend that builds to static files is a site, not an app: build it with a relative base
(Vite `base: './'`) and link the build folder ([sites.md](sites.md)).

A tool that lets visitors run code (Jupyter, `marimo edit`, a shell, an eval endpoint) is out
of scope: tell the user it waits on the sandboxed setup in lantern's `TODO.md` (Phase 6).

## Kind

Pick one; each is one command.

- **Server** (`lantern add-app <name>`): lantern runs it; you write `run.sh`. Everything from
  § Survey on is about this kind.
- **Tunnel** (`lantern add-tunnel <name> <ssh-host> <host:port>`): a service only reachable
  through ssh. `<host:port>` is the target as the ssh host sees it; `<ssh-host>` is
  `user@host`, `ssh://user@host:port`, or a `Host` alias from `~/.ssh/config` (prefer an
  alias that already matches). The CLI writes `run.sh` (an `ssh -N -L` forward). The unit has
  no terminal or agent, so `ssh -o BatchMode=yes <ssh-host> true` must succeed: if it doesn't,
  the user runs `ssh-copy-id` themselves (it asks for their password: never ask for it,
  store it, or script it).
- **Proxy** (`lantern add-proxy <name> <host:port>`): a plain-HTTP service this machine
  reaches directly (`curl -sI http://<host:port>/` answers). Nothing runs, no unit. An HTTPS
  upstream isn't supported by the CLI: say so in the report.

## Mount

- **strip** (default): served at `/<name>/`, Caddy removes the prefix; the app sees `/…` and
  gets the prefix in `X-Forwarded-Prefix`. For apps with relative URLs, or apps told their root.
- **keep** (`--keep-prefix`): served at `/<name>/` with the full path passed through. For
  frameworks that serve under a configured base path themselves.
- **own port** (`--own-port`): served at the root of `http://<host>:<lan-port>/`, port from
  8201–8299; `/<name>/` redirects there. For apps that need `/` and can't be told otherwise:
  device and vendor web UIs (cameras, NVRs, routers, admin dashboards), SPAs built with base
  `/`. Usually right for tunnels and proxies.

Survey a service you can't change: `curl -s http://<upstream>/ | grep -oE '(href|src|action)="/[^"]*"'`
and `curl -sI` for a `Location: /…` redirect. Any hit means own port. For a tunnel target,
run the same through ssh (`ssh <ssh-host> curl -s http://<host:port>/`) when the user's key
login already works; otherwise default to own port. Browsers share cookies across the ports
of one host: two apps on their own ports that use the same cookie name (two cameras of one
model) log each other out. Mention it when that applies.

## Survey

- **Entry point**: how the user runs it today (README, Makefile, scripts, `pyproject.toml`,
  `package.json`).
- **Run command**, bound to `127.0.0.1:$PORT`:
  - Python goes through uv: `uv run --project <repo> …` (has `pyproject.toml`),
    `uv run --with-requirements <repo>/requirements.txt …`, or `uv run --script app.py`
    (single file with a PEP 723 header).
  - Other languages: the app's own toolchain, already installed.
- **Load**: heavy dependencies (torch, CUDA, large models) go in the proposal with their
  RAM/GPU cost; the machine is shared.
- **Secrets**: env files stay in the app's repo; `run.sh` sources them
  (`set -a; . <repo>/.env; set +a`).
- **Mount**: from § Mount and the table below.
- **Absolute URLs**: grep templates, static files and JS for root-relative URLs (`href="/`,
  `src="/`, `action="/`, `fetch("/`, redirects to `"/…"`). In strip mode each one leaves
  `/<name>/` unless the framework adds the prefix itself; when there's no flag for it, use
  `--own-port`.
- **Home**: an app with no repo of its own keeps its code in `$(lantern content)/apps/<name>/`.

Prefer fixes in `run.sh` (flags, env, a wrapper) over edits to the app; show any code edit as
a diff in the proposal.

| Framework | Mode | In `run.sh` |
|---|---|---|
| Flask / Werkzeug | strip | `ProxyFix(app.wsgi_app, x_prefix=1)` so `url_for` adds the prefix (wrapper below) |
| FastAPI / Starlette | strip | `uvicorn mod:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port "$PORT" --root-path "/$APP_NAME"` |
| Gradio | strip | env `GRADIO_ROOT_PATH="/$APP_NAME" GRADIO_SERVER_NAME=127.0.0.1 GRADIO_SERVER_PORT="$PORT"`, when `launch()` doesn't hardcode them |
| Streamlit | keep | `streamlit run app.py --server.address 127.0.0.1 --server.port "$PORT" --server.baseUrlPath "$APP_NAME" --server.headless true` |
| marimo (`run`) | keep | `marimo run app.py --host 127.0.0.1 --port "$PORT" --base-url "/$APP_NAME" --headless` |
| Dash | keep | env `DASH_URL_BASE_PATHNAME="$BASE_PATH"`, server on `127.0.0.1:$PORT` |
| Django (gunicorn) | keep | env `SCRIPT_NAME="/$APP_NAME"`; `STATIC_URL` under the prefix |
| anything else | strip | relative URLs only; own port when it hardcodes `/` |

Flask wrapper, all inside `run.sh`:

```bash
cd /path/to/repo
exec uv run --project . python - <<'PY'
import os
from werkzeug.middleware.proxy_fix import ProxyFix
from app import app  # the repo's Flask app object
app.wsgi_app = ProxyFix(app.wsgi_app, x_prefix=1)
app.run(host="127.0.0.1", port=int(os.environ["PORT"]))
PY
```

## Exposure

A tunnel or proxy puts a service from another host or network on the LAN, and lantern adds
no login of its own. The proposal names the service, whether it has its own login, and
that anyone who can reach lantern can reach it. Caddy sends requests to a non-loopback
upstream through `HTTP_PROXY` in `$LANTERN_ROOT/lantern.env` unless `NO_PROXY` covers its
host: when lantern.env sets a proxy, say which way the upstream will go.

## Run

1. The kind's command, with the mount flag.
2. Server: write `apps/<name>/run.sh` (keep its header comment, `set -euo pipefail`, `cd` to
   the app, `exec` the server). Tunnel and proxy: leave `run.sh` as written. Every kind: fill
   `title`/`description` in `apps/<name>/README.md`.
3. Server and tunnel: `systemctl --user enable --now lantern-app@<name>`. A first start can
   take minutes while uv installs dependencies: re-run `lantern check <name>` until the app
   answers, and read `journalctl --user -u lantern-app@<name> -n 50` when it doesn't. Units
   don't see the shell's environment: a start stuck on `Downloading …` while the shell has
   `HTTPS_PROXY` set means those proxy variables belong in `$LANTERN_ROOT/lantern.env`
   (`lantern doctor` flags it); add them in the proposal, then
   `systemctl --user restart lantern-app@<name>`. A tunnel that won't come up is almost
   always key login: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes <ssh-host> true`.
4. `lantern check <name>`: a `401` (the app's own login) counts as answering.
5. `lantern rm-app <name>` undoes it all (unit stopped and disabled, wrapper removed).

# Apps

An app is a process lantern proxies at `/<name>/`. Lantern's `apps/<name>/` is a machine-local
wrapper (gitignored): `run.sh` (start command), `app.env` (`PORT`), `route.caddy` and
`README.md` (landing card: `title`, `description`). The systemd user unit
`lantern-app@<name>` runs `run.sh` from that folder with `PORT`, `APP_NAME` and
`BASE_PATH=/<name>/` set. `$LANTERN_ROOT/apps/_example-app/` is a working example.

A frontend that builds to static files is a site, not an app: build it with a relative base
(Vite `base: './'`) and link the build folder ([sites.md](sites.md)).

A tool that lets visitors run code (Jupyter, `marimo edit`, a shell, an eval endpoint) is out
of scope: tell the user it waits on the sandboxed setup in lantern's `TODO.md` (Phase 6).

## Survey

- **Entry point**: how the user runs it today (README, Makefile, scripts, `pyproject.toml`,
  `package.json`).
- **Run command**, bound to `127.0.0.1:$PORT`:
  - Python goes through uv: `uv run --project <repo> …` (has `pyproject.toml`),
    `uv run --with-requirements <repo>/requirements.txt …`, or `uv run --script app.py`
    (single file with a PEP 723 header).
  - Other languages: the app's own toolchain, already installed.
- **Load**: heavy dependencies (torch, CUDA, large models) go in the proposal with their
  RAM/GPU cost; the machine is shared.
- **Secrets**: env files stay in the app's repo; `run.sh` sources them
  (`set -a; . <repo>/.env; set +a`).
- **Prefix mode**: from the table below.
- **Absolute URLs**: grep templates, static files and JS for root-relative URLs (`href="/`,
  `src="/`, `action="/`, `fetch("/`, redirects to `"/…"`). In strip mode each one leaves
  `/<name>/` unless the framework adds the prefix itself.
- **Home**: an app with no repo of its own keeps its code in `$(lantern content)/apps/<name>/`.

Prefer fixes in `run.sh` (flags, env, a wrapper) over edits to the app; show any code edit as
a diff in the proposal.

## Prefix

- **strip** (`lantern add-app <name>`): Caddy removes `/<name>`; the app sees `/…` and gets
  the prefix in `X-Forwarded-Prefix`. For apps with relative URLs, or apps told their root path.
- **keep** (`lantern add-app <name> --keep-prefix`): the app sees the full `/<name>/…`. For
  frameworks that serve under a configured base path themselves.

| Framework | Mode | In `run.sh` |
|---|---|---|
| Flask / Werkzeug | strip | `ProxyFix(app.wsgi_app, x_prefix=1)` so `url_for` adds the prefix (wrapper below) |
| FastAPI / Starlette | strip | `uvicorn mod:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port "$PORT" --root-path "/$APP_NAME"` |
| Gradio | strip | env `GRADIO_ROOT_PATH="/$APP_NAME" GRADIO_SERVER_NAME=127.0.0.1 GRADIO_SERVER_PORT="$PORT"`, when `launch()` doesn't hardcode them |
| Streamlit | keep | `streamlit run app.py --server.address 127.0.0.1 --server.port "$PORT" --server.baseUrlPath "$APP_NAME" --server.headless true` |
| marimo (`run`) | keep | `marimo run app.py --host 127.0.0.1 --port "$PORT" --base-url "/$APP_NAME" --headless` |
| Dash | keep | env `DASH_URL_BASE_PATHNAME="$BASE_PATH"`, server on `127.0.0.1:$PORT` |
| Django (gunicorn) | keep | env `SCRIPT_NAME="/$APP_NAME"`; `STATIC_URL` under the prefix |
| anything else | strip | relative URLs only |

Flask wrapper, all inside `run.sh`:

```bash
cd /path/to/repo
exec uv run --project . python - <<'PY'
import os
from werkzeug.middleware.proxy_fix import ProxyFix
from app import app  # the repo's Flask app object
app.wsgi_app = ProxyFix(app.wsgi_app, x_prefix=1)
app.run(host="127.0.0.1", port=int(os.environ["PORT"]))
PY
```

## Run

1. `lantern add-app <name>`, with `--keep-prefix` for keep mode.
2. Write `apps/<name>/run.sh`: keep its header comment, `set -euo pipefail`, `cd` to the app,
   `exec` the server. Fill `title`/`description` in `apps/<name>/README.md`.
3. `systemctl --user enable --now lantern-app@<name>`. A first start can take minutes while
   uv installs dependencies: re-run `lantern check <name>` until the app answers, and read
   `journalctl --user -u lantern-app@<name> -n 50` when it doesn't. Units don't see the
   shell's environment: a start stuck on `Downloading …` while the shell has `HTTPS_PROXY`
   set means those proxy variables belong in `$LANTERN_ROOT/lantern.env` (`lantern doctor`
   flags it); add them in the proposal, then `systemctl --user restart lantern-app@<name>`.
4. `lantern rm-app <name>` undoes it all (unit stopped and disabled, wrapper removed).

content.text:
Own-port mounting, `add-tunnel` and `add-proxy` are built and live. The frp dashboard works through lantern. The tunnel is set up but can't start until your ssh key is installed on the jump host.

**How it fits together:** an app has a **kind** and a **mount**.
- **Kind:**
  - **server:** `add-app`; you write `run.sh`. Unchanged.
  - **tunnel:** `add-tunnel <name> <ssh-host> <host:port>`; it writes `run.sh` for you as an `ssh -N -L` forward that systemd restarts if it drops.
  - **proxy:** `add-proxy <name> <host:port>`; nothing runs, so there's no unit.
- **Mount:**
  - `/<name>/` with the prefix stripped (the default);
  - `/<name>/` with the prefix kept (`--keep-prefix`);
  - **its own port** (`--own-port`, from 8201–8299), where the app owns `/` and `/<name>/` redirects there.

`add-app`'s default output is unchanged, and existing apps like `jcj-relabel` keep the same Caddy snippets.

**Your two apps:**
- **`frp-dashboard`** at http://192.168.1.10:8201/: `lantern check` passes, and your browser will show frp's login prompt.
- **`zitong-shiyinqi`** at http://192.168.1.10:8202/: ssh still rejects key login for `teamhd` on `:12303`. To finish it, run these yourself (the first asks for the password once):
  ```
  ! ssh-copy-id -p 12303 teamhd@8.156.94.43
  ! systemctl --user enable --now lantern-app@zitong-shiyinqi
  ```
  Then `lantern check zitong-shiyinqi` should pass. Until then, port 8202 shows lantern's "isn't reachable" page.

I picked both names from the evidence. Port 7500 and `realm="Restricted"` look like frp's dashboard, and `10.97.12.86` is the 识音器 in your zitong table. To rename one, run `rm-app` and add it again.

**On the landing page:** a green dot means the app goes through an ssh tunnel, and a blue dot means it's proxied from another host. An app on its own port shows `:8201/` instead of `/name/`, so it doesn't get its own dot. There's a small legend under "Apps", and hovering a dot shows the target. One thing to watch: the green dot sits next to the green "up" badge and could be confused with it. Changing a colour is one CSS line.

**Two problems I hit and fixed:**
- **Proxy loop.** Caddy follows the `HTTP_PROXY` in `lantern.env`, so remote requests go through your mihomo proxy on `:8897`. Caddy was passing on the visitor's `Host` header, and mihomo routes by that header, so it sent each request back to Caddy. The result was a `431` error and a false "up" badge. A proxied service now gets its own `Host`; servers and tunnels keep the visitor's.
- **Caddy parse bug.** A snippet that imports another snippet breaks the config once it's used twice. All snippets are now written out in full, and I checked a config with 16 apps covering every kind and mount.

Both are recorded in CLAUDE.md.

**Tests:** 80 of 81 smoke tests pass, including 29 new ones. The one failure comes from your uncommitted heading edit in [sites/_example/README.md](sites/_example/README.md): the test expects `<h1 id="lantern-example">`, so either update the test or revert the heading. `lantern doctor` reports all good.

**Exposure:** the frp dashboard can list everything frps forwards, and its own login is now the only thing protecting it on the LAN. The same goes for the camera UI once the tunnel is up.

**Not done:**
- HTTPS upstreams such as the ISC platform on `:1443`. They need `tls_insecure_skip_verify`, so I listed this in [TODO.md](TODO.md).
- I couldn't read the firewall settings without root. If ufw is on, ports 8201–8299 need opening.
- Nothing for subdomains.
- Optional: requests to `8.156.94.43` go through mihomo, so they stop if mihomo does. Adding that IP to `NO_PROXY` in `lantern.env` makes them direct, which I confirmed works.

Everything is uncommitted. In the lantern repo I changed [Caddyfile](Caddyfile), [bin/lantern](bin/lantern), [_shared/index.html](_shared/index.html), [_shared/error.html](_shared/error.html), [_shared/style.css](_shared/style.css), [skill/SKILL.md](skill/SKILL.md), [skill/apps.md](skill/apps.md), [README.md](README.md), [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md), [TODO.md](TODO.md) and [tests/smoke.sh](tests/smoke.sh). The two app folders under `apps/` are gitignored and local to this machine.

# port) holds one import line written by bin/lantern. Snippets don't import each other:

# and with the visitor's Host a forward proxy sends the request right back here.

**1. Login prompt on the landing page.** It came from the up/down badge. The badge sends `HEAD /_status/frp-dashboard`, frp answers `401` with a `WWW-Authenticate: Basic` header, and the browser opens a login dialog for that even on a background request.

- **All apps:** every app's badge uses this route now, path-mounted ones included, so this can't come back with a password-protected app on `/<name>/`. Existing apps like `jcj-relabel` picked it up through the Caddy snippets with no file changes.
- **`lantern check`** now fails if an app's badge would prompt.

Reload the landing page and the dialog should be gone.

Tunnel.** Key login works, so I started `lantern-app@zitong-shiyinqi`. `lantern check zitong-shiyinqi` passes, and the 识音器 UI answers at http://192.168.1.10:8202/. systemd will restart the tunnel if it drops. I've only checked that the first page loads (`200`), so please try logging in and using the device UI in the browser.

jcj-relabel works again at **http://192.168.1.10:8080/jcj-relabel/**. systemd now runs it on port 8765, and `lantern check jcj-relabel` passes.

**Why it wasn't working:**
- **Nothing was running on lantern's side.** The `jcj-relabel` wrapper was created this morning with port 8101, but its systemd unit was never started. The relabel you were using was a copy you started by hand on Oct 19, on port 8765, which lantern didn't know about. So lantern proxied to an empty port and got `502`.
- **My bug made it worse.** While my Caddyfile had the nested-snippet parse bug, the app's `route.caddy` was hand-edited from `lantern-app` to `lantern-proxy` to get around it. After my `Host` fix, that snippet would have sent relabel `Host: 127.0.0.1:…`, which relabel's allowed-host check rejects.

**What I did:**
- **Stopped your hand-started copy.** Its terminal will show it exited.
- **Recreated `jcj-relabel` on port 8765** through the CLI, kept your `run.sh` and `README.md`, and started the unit.
- **Kept the frp path working.** The new copy listens on 127.0.0.1 only, so `192.168.1.10:8765` no longer answers directly; use the lantern URL. The frp address `http://8.156.94.43:12302/` still returns `200`, so `frpc` reaches it fine.

  - relabel doesn't implement `HEAD` and answers `501`, so its badge would have shown "down". The badge route now asks apps with `GET`.

- **Added a `doctor` warning** for an app on 127.0.0.1 that's routed with `lantern-proxy`.

`lantern doctor` warns that 8765 is outside 8101–8199. That's expected since you chose it, and harmless.

**Your question:** yes. `lantern add-proxy <name> 127.0.0.1:<port>` points at something you keep running yourself; lantern starts nothing and creates no unit. Before this change, it would have sent a local app like relabel the wrong `Host`. Now any 127.0.0.1 target gets the visitor's `Host`, the same as an app lantern runs, and no blue "another host" dot. The skill describes this, and suggests letting lantern run a local process instead, because nothing restarts a proxied one if it dies.

content.text:
Both changes are live. jcj-relabel's login is yours to test.

**1. jcj-relabel on its own port:** http://192.168.1.10:8203/
- **What changed:** relabel now owns `/` there, so its login redirects and session cookie no longer go through `/jcj-relabel/`. The old address `/jcj-relabel/` on 8080 redirects to the new port. Still on 127.0.0.1:8765 under systemd.
- **`run.sh`:** now allows `192.168.1.10:8203` instead of `:8080`. The frp address (`8.156.94.43:12302`) still answers `200`; relabel allows it through its own config.
- **One thing to watch:** browsers don't separate cookies by port. If logging into relabel ever logs you out of the 识音器 UI on :8202, or the other way round, they're using the same cookie name.
- **Badge fix along the way:** for local apps on their own port, the badge now sends the `Host` a real visit to that port would. Before, relabel answered it `403`. I updated the tunnel app's route the same way.

`lantern check` passes for all three apps.

**2. New tabs:** every doc and app card on the landing page now opens in a new tab (`target="_blank" rel="noopener"`). Links inside docs are unchanged.

**Skill change:** I'm holding this until you've tested the login. Once you confirm own-port fixed it, I'll change the skill so the app proposal asks you to choose: a path under lantern's main page (`/<name>/`, needs prefix-safe URLs) or a dedicated port (the app owns `/`, safest for logins and absolute URLs). It will still state which one the survey points to.

All 96 smoke tests pass. Repo files changed this round, uncommitted: [bin/lantern](bin/lantern), [Caddyfile](Caddyfile) (comment only), [_shared/index.html](_shared/index.html), [tests/smoke.sh](tests/smoke.sh) and [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md). Under `apps/` I also changed `jcj-relabel/` (`app.env`, `run.sh`, `route.caddy`, `port.caddy`) and `zitong-shiyinqi/route.caddy`.
